name: 1099 String Quartet - Late Beethoven Quartets at Wicker

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Treat yourself to the 1099 String Quartet (Professional Ensemble) performing LIVE at Wicker Park! This year, the quartet led by Ryan Loeckel (Artistic Director) will present 3 of the Late Beethoven String Quartets: String Quartet No. 14 in C sharp minor, Op. 131 (1826) (Performed 6/25 at 11am), String Quartet No. 15 in A minor, Op. 132 (1825) (Performed 8/6 at 11am), String Quartet No. 16 in F major, Op. 135 (1826) (Performed 8/27 at 11am). Ryan Loeckel will give both musical and historic notes on the music performed. Bring a Blanket and Picnic. Performer BIOS & Details: www.WickerPark.org

name: 2 Day: South Side Skating Academy at Morgan Park SC

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: The South Side Skating Academy is a Bridge Program, for skaters looking to Bridge the gap between recreational Learn to Skate, and starting to become a competitive skater. The Academy is for skaters in Pre-Free Skate through Free Skate 3, and is made up of multiple classes (on and off the ice) each week, for a reduced rate. Skaters in the Bridge Program will be enrolled in this structured training program, with the goal to join the MPSC Competitive Team. Cost (if registered for 2 more sessions) also includes a Membership Team Jacket, and other activities.

name: 2027 Herbie Hancock Fellows at Marquette

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Join the Marquette Park Cultural Center for a free concert! In fall 2025, six extraordinary young jazz musicians from around the world were selected for the Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz Performance at UCLA, Class of 2027. These excellent players study deeply as individuals and as a small group—receiving personal mentoring, ensemble coaching, and lectures on the jazz tradition from the legends of the jazz tradition. Beyond that, they are charged to experiment in expanding jazz in new directions through their compositions and performances. Herbie Hancock Fellows have performed in Saint Petersburg, Russia; Havana, Cuba; Melbourne, Sydney and Mt. Gambier, Australia; at the celebration commemorating the 40th anniversary of the coronation of the King of Thailand, the 1998 Summit of the Americas in Chile before 34 heads of state, the United Nations “Day of Philosophy” event in Paris sponsored by UNESCO, and the Tokyo Jazz Festival. The students have also participated in tours of Argentina, China, Egypt, India, Morocco, Peru, Russia, Vietnam and, most recently, Jordan with Institute Chairman Herbie Hancock. These musicians’ concepts and playing will come to define the sound of jazz well into the future. Come get an early glimpse into what that jazz will sound like. The Hancock Fellows will come to the Marquette Park Cultural Center on April 28th at 4:30 for a free show in its historic auditorium. This unprecedented performance has come to the Southwest Side as a part of International Jazz Day celebrations, hosted this year by the City of Chicago. Free admission! Nicolaus Gelin: trumpet Nathan Gilbreath: trombone Mwanzi Harriott: guitar Yerin Kim: bass Elisee Ngbo: piano Mailo Rakotonanahary: drums

name: 312 Grit at Jefferson

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: 312 Grit is a functional fitness and personal development program designed for individuals who aspire to elevate their health, performance, and overall quality of life. The program integrates high-level functional training with education in proper nutrition and intentional character development, creating a well-rounded approach to long-term success. At its core, 312 Grit focuses on improving sports performance, strength, conditioning, mobility, and resilience through purposeful, scalable workouts. Beyond physical training, participants are guided in building sustainable nutrition habits that support performance, recovery, and lifelong wellness. What sets 312 Grit apart is its emphasis on developing the character traits of tomorrow’s leaders: discipline, accountability, grit, teamwork, and integrity. Through mentorship, structured competition, and shared challenges, athletes learn to push beyond comfort while supporting one another in a team-centered environment. 312 Grit is more than a workout class; it is a mentoring-driven community where individuals are challenged to grow physically, mentally, and emotionally. The program prepares participants not only to perform at a higher level in sport, but to lead with confidence, resilience, and purpose in every area of life.

name: A Mothers Day Adventure! at Northerly Island

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Celebrate mom’s wild side and have an adventure at Northerly Island Park! Moms and their families can enjoy activities like archery, fishing, live reptile encounters, birds of prey with Wings and Things, arts & crafts, nature play, and a mom-focused nature walk. Mothers’ Day Adventure is a family event with activities for all-ages, however archery and fishing are only available for children 8+. All child participants must have a parent or guardian supervising. Activities are both inside and outside, please dress for the weather.

name: A Multi-ethnic Ode to Autumn at McKinley

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: A vibrant showcase featuring a diverse array of singing, dancing, fashion shows, and other forms of performing arts will be presented by artists from the Chinese, Hispanic, and Black communities. This event is organized by the Chicago Chinese Culture & Arts Society (CCCAS) and will take place on a stage in McKinley Park. It aims to celebrate the rich abundance of the autumn harvest, promote the joy of interracial harmony, and express hopes for the United States as it approaches its 250th birthday. https://www.chicagochineseculture.com

name: A Place to Play Summit at South Shore

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The Sport for Good Chicago coalition has partnered with the Chicago Park District to host “A Place to Play” – a one-day summit discussing the role that public space activation plays in building a safer city. During this day, stakeholders across the city will have a chance to learn from expert researchers and practitioners, exchange success stories, and work with one another to explore the unique power we all have in moving this work forward. This event is for visionary leaders who are committed to imagining a city where young people and their families are able to use their public spaces to sustain a strong community, move their bodies and feel safe to play. You have been invited to this event because you play a role in bringing that vision to life. We hope to see you there.

name: A Spanish Summer at Berger

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: In collaboration with EnsAmble Ad-Hoc directors Francy Acosta and José Luis Posada, the Bach and Beethoven Experience is thrilled to present A Spanish Summer, featuring music of Colombia and Venezuela. Through romances, ballads, dance tunes, working songs, milking songs, coffee songs, and counting songs, this program depicts a day in the life of summer in Colombia. Alongside BBE directors Brandi Berry Benson (violin) and Leighann Daihl Ragusa (flute), directors Francy and José Luis will be joined by members of EnsAmble Ad-Hoc on various instruments including vocals, guitar, tiple, cuatro, and bass. This family-friendly program will also encourage audience participation!

name: AACM Future Explorations at Fred Anderson

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: This year the AACM would like to celebrate the future of our Great Black Music tradition, ancient to the future. We will feature compositions from three of our youngest members- Adam Zanolini, Alexis Lombre, and Angel Bat Dawid. Their development as musicians and composers has been nurtured by the inter-generational ensemble of the AACM's Great Black Music Ensemble. These three emerging composers draw upon traditional forms of African American music and music from the African diaspora. These musicians push boldly into radically unknown territory, creating future explorations of the outer realms. This event is presented as a part of the City of Chicago’s 2020 Year of Chicago Music. Experience music in the key of Chicago at www.YearofChicagoMusic.org .

name: Adult Martial Arts & Self Defense at Morgan Park SC

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Our Martial Arts program will build on the skills that focuses on the self-defense and Kung Fu. The curriculum includes conflict resolution and non-lethal restraint. Skills include blocks, kicks, punches, falls and throws. All students receive a study sheet that will assist parents in reviewing the material. The class also works on flexibility, running, endurance, strength, concentration and coordination. Students will perform exercises such as jogging, jumping jacks, lunges, and push ups. All students will begin with a warmup; if student is tardy, they will still have a quick warmup to prepare their body for class activity. Participants are able to sign up for more than one class for additional practice and develop stronger technique

name: Adult Modern Partnership at Berger

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Kristina Fluty leads this modern dance class for advanced and professional dancers, hosted by Arts Partner Synapse Arts. Kristina has been teaching and dancing in Chicago for the past two decades. Her main creative home since 2003 is molly Shanahan/Mad Shak, and she is currently completing the inaugural Spiral Body Techniques teacher certification with Shanahan. She is an Associate Professor at The Theatre School at DePaul, where she teaches movement to actors. Her dance class prioritizes pleasure and honoring/embracing how you move right now. It is also anchored by Fluty's certification in Laban/Bartenieff Movement Analysis and her many years of Feldenkrais personal study. Class will likely begin on the floor with gentle developmental movement phases, then evolve out into dancing with delicious complexity, spatial clarity, and ease.

name: Adult Swimming and Sports (Special Rec) at Mt. Greenwood

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: For individuals with a primary intellectual or developmental disability. Participants will learn basic swimming techniques, advanced breathing techniques, and mechanics of the four basic strokes (freestyle, backstroke, butterfly and breaststroke). Participants will be grouped according to skill level. Learn to play a variety of sports and brush up on skills. Instructors teach and reinforce skills development through drills and game play, with a concentration on sportsmanship and friendly competition. Sports vary by season.

name: Adult Wheelchair Basketball at Jesse White

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: For individuals with a primary physical disability. The Chicago Skyhawks are a partnership with the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab (SRALab) and the Chicago Park District for individuals with a primary physical disability to play the amazing game of wheelchair basketball. Through individual and team drills athletes will raise their level of play and gain an understanding of the game. The Skyhawks compete in the National Wheelchair Basketball Association (NWBA) Division III at regional tournaments and events. Indoor wheelchair softball practice will begin on April 9th.

name: Adult Wheelchair Softball at California

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Wheelchair Softball is one of the premier sport choices for members of Chicago's adaptive sports community. The program is for people with a primary physical disability to come out and take part in Chicago's sport of choice at Cubs Care Field at California Park; which was one of the first fields in the United States designed for play in the National Wheelchair Softball Association (NWSA). Currently there are two teams of athletes in the program who compete in tournaments throughout the area and if they qualify will move onto the national tournament. For more information please contact Special Recreation Adaptive Sport Program & Event Coordinator Daniel Ferreira for more information: daniel.ferreira@chicagoparkdistrict.com

name: Afro-Caribbean Maypole: Woven Culture at Columbus

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: This event has been canceled due to weather. We look forward to rescheduling on another date.Through dance and rooted rhythms, A 3D Canvas of Woven Culture will take you into a merry-go-round of weaving and unweaving, circling and uncircling, braiding and unbraiding the colors and history of Afro-Caribbean and European exchange through the Maypole dance. You will be invited to dance and wrap to lively Afro-Caribbean drumming and song. The activity will be circled by dance, song, and music representing many of the Afro-Caribbean islands... get a glimpse of the unique performance art traditions. Perhaps it'll help you decide your next vacation. Wherever you go, don't forget your ribbon to show them" what you've got .... trained and true by the West Indian Dance Theater Company of Chicago! https://www.facebook.com/WIDTC

name: AfroSoul Yoga Drum Circle at Euclid

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: A two part event starting with an all inclusive drum circle. The Drum Circle leader gives a brief history on the Djembe, then leads participants through basic rhythms they can play during the dance portion of the event. The 2nd portion is an invigorating, fun for all ages, DANCE focused YOGA. Lively sounds of drums and soul stirring BASS, participants will "DANCE YOUR WAY TO NAMASTE"™? with movements from across the African Diaspora. As an active meditation, all the principles and intention of yoga are the foundation. The dance portion is not about learning the dances to proficiency but using the repetitive movement, freeing your mind and using the breath work needed to execute the various combos to achieve your yoga. In accordance with Be Safe Chicago Guidelines for Parks and Recreation Activities, participants in this activity will be required to wear a mask and practice social distancing at all times while participating. Patrons who are exhibiting any symptoms of COVID-19 are asked to stay home and join us for an event when symptoms subside.

name: Alex in Windyland at Homan Square

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Alex in Windyland is a new play about the complexities of the foster care system. The day before her 12th birthday, Alex is taken from her sister and transported onto a train called Windyland. Windyland is a magical liminal space where Alex faces new challenges, finds new friends, and goes on adventures. Will Alex be reunited with her sister? Will she find a forever home? The clock is ticking, and the train keeps running. As the train speeds forward, the urgency of her situation becomes clear, just as it does for thousands of foster youth navigating an unpredictable system.

name: America: Songs of Protest and Freedom at Clarendon

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: 2026 marks the 250th anniversary of the United States. America: Songs and Stories of Protest and Freedom is a multi-genre concert of spoken word and music. It’s written and narrated by award-winning journalist, Cheryl Corley, and features a stellar band lead by singer/songwriter Lucy Smith. The concert chronicles America’s story from its founding years to the 21st century. It includes Walt Whitman’s “I Hear America Singing” along with the words of other American authors. Songs include: Curtis Mayfield’s “This is My Country”, John Lennon’s “Imagine,” and Beyonce’s “Freedom.” It is a performance that presents the intricacies of America’s 250 years.

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: American Choral Classics celebrates the richness and range of the American choral tradition, bringing together music by a wonderfully diverse group of American composers. Spanning poetry, folk song, spirituals, protest, and hymn-inspired reflection, the program explores the many voices that shape America’s musical identity, personal and communal, searching and joyful, deeply rooted and always evolving. description: A medley of singing, dancing, a fashion show, and other forms of performing arts will be staged to celebrate, in the traditionally oriental way, the family-reuniting festival, one of the grandest festivities honored throughout Asian countries. name: An Introduction to Shamanism at McFetridge

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Meet Your Power Animal & Learn to Journey: An Introduction to Shamanism Introduce yourself to modern Shamanism and its worldwide origins; A way of life combining earthly traditions and spiritual practices teaching us to walk in both worlds. Learn the basic skills of the meditative practice known as Shamanic Journeying: - Create a Sacred Circle - Meet your Power Animal - This Spirit Guide may be a new surprise or an old friend - Journey together to non-ordinary reality - Connect more deeply to Spirit to receive Divine Guidance - Acknowledge your true self and her/his needs - Access information to help you unlock healing relief on many levels By bringing the teachings of shamanism into our daily lives, we can more fully experience our own Divinity, our innate connection to the web of life and dream a new dream for ourselves and the world. Awaken knowledge from deep within you to support "remembering" the Journey of Our Soul. What to bring: Wear comfortable clothing since meditations can be seated or lying down as well as a special blanket or sheet to be on/wrap yourself in and an eye covering (mask or scarf) to help you create a sacred focused space. Other things to bring if you?re called are something sacred to place on the altar, a journal to jot down your insights, a hand drum, or rattle. Please let me know ahead of time if you have a breathing issue which would prevent a smoke smudge since we have an easy alternative. Questions? Contact Monica at (773) 310-1228 or MonicaMoonPlace@gmail.com *Class will be cancelled if 3 participant minimum is not met 3 days prior*

name: Anatomical Circus at Sherman

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Chicago Rewilding Society presents "'Anatomical Circus", an installation of life-size anatomical educational dioramas, anatomical face painting, and animal-assisted therapy with fantastically painted creatures. Anatomical Circus explores our internal and external landscapes, invigorating audiences to celebrate and understand their own humanness through wonder, delight & a sense of magic.

name: Anchor Curatorial Residency Info Session at Ellis

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Join us for an Anchor Curatorial Residency Info Session at Ellis Park to learn more about the residency, meet the park staff, and ask questions. To learn more or to apply to be the 2026-2027 Anchor Curator-in-Residence, please visit this site.

name: Anchor Residency Welcome Reception at Ellis

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: We invite you to celebrate and meet Lional "Brother El" Freeman at the Anchor Residency Curator Welcome Reception at Ellis Park on Thursday, May 21, from 5:30 to 7:30 pm. Starting at 5:30 pm, you’ll have the chance to mingle with the curator, enjoy local bites from Carver 47, and connect with fellow community members. The evening will culminate with a panel at 6:00 pm featuring past and present Anchor collaborators, and we’ll have the grand debut of our Anchor Monograph! RSVP for event through this link . This monograph, which was published at the end of last year, is now ready to make its way out into the world for you, dear readers. It builds on the success of previous residencies at Austin Town Hall Park and Marquette Park. In partnership with Sixty Inches From Center, an online art publication, the publication critically engages with the residency’s learnings and outcomes, highlighting how municipalities can empower culture workers to address community harm through public/private partnerships. Supported by a grant from the Terra Foundation in 2024 and additional support from the Builder’s Initiative, the monograph was edited by multidisciplinary artist Kamilah Rashied. Anchor Curatorial Residency is a funded Chicago Park District community-driven curatorial residency that rotates among the Chicago Park District’s Cultural Centers. ** About Lional "Brother El" Freeman Brother El is a Chicago-based social practice artist, spontaneous composer, audio engineer, and educator whose work bridges music, community engagement, and public space. Rooted in hip-hop, DIY culture, and South Side Chicago, he is known for his improvised Live PA performances using drum machines, samplers, and synthesizers. He also founded The Beat Bank and creates dynamic public art events, such as Sandbox Symphony, transforming spaces into vibrant, community-centered cultural hubs. Through his work, Brother El expands access to art, uplifts youth and artist communities, and inspires creative possibility. We can’t wait to see his vision come to life at Ellis Park!

name: Angel Bat Dawid at Jackson Park

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The Art Institute of Chicago presents a performance by Chicago clarinetist and composer Angel Bat Dawid in Jackson Park. Bat Dawid performs her original five-movement suite titled Peace: A Suite for Sky Landing, a Mended Petal Odyssey, composed in response to Yoko Ono’s Skylanding. Bat Dawid performs with the Cosmic Space Arkestra. This event is presented as a part of the City of Chicago’s 2020 Year of Chicago Music. Experience music in the key of Chicago at www.YearofChicagoMusic.org .

name: Animal Tales at Big Marsh

age_range.raw_age_text: Age less than 6 yrs

description: Join the Chicago Public Library, Vodak-East Side Branch at Big Marsh Park for a 30-minute nature-inspired story time directly followed by a 30-minute complementary activity. Activities could include meeting an animal, going on a nature hike, and exploring loose parts and sensory stations. This program is open to all youth and families. Registration is encouraged; walk-ins are welcome. Come early or stay late to explore the nearly 300-acre Natural Area and Bike Park that is Big Marsh Park.

name: Annual Bike Rally at The 606

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The Third Annual 606 Bike Rally is a collaboration with the Chicago Police Department's 14th and 25th Districts, West Town Bikes and other local community organizations. The rally is a fun, free event that engages and encourages bicycle riders of all ages and abilities. Bike-focused resource partners set up at both the east and west ends of The 606 and provide a wide range of free resources: everything from healthy snacks, tune-ups, quick tutorials, helmet fittings, light and bike bell giveaways, and bike maps and guides are all available. Adding to the festive spirit of the event are bike decorating stations, obstacle courses, a bike washing area and live music from local school bands. This event is free and open to the public.

name: Annual Plant Sale at Kilbourn

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The 28th Annual Plant Sale will be held in-person at the Kilbourn Park Greenhouse. You can view the list of plants here. Kilbourn Park Greenhouse will offer more than 150 varieties of organically-grown vegetable, herb, edible flower seedlings and so much more. Customers can expect a wide variety of open-pollinated and heirloom tomatoes, peppers, and eggplants. Other highlights include an assortment of herbs, greens and onions. These seedlings are grown with the support of a team of dedicated volunteers who make this Plant Sale possible. Volunteers will be on hand to answer questions about plant selection and planting. This yearly fundraiser supports the greenhouse and our work to connect kids to nature and healthy foods. Also available at the plant sale: Perennials and other plants donated by volunteers of the Kilbourn Park Organic Greenhouse, compost, and bake sale items. Look for the Friends of Kilbourn Park Organic Greenhouse tables just outside the main gate to the gardens. Cost: Free Admission, Plant Prices $4. | cash and credit accepted. We suggest that you bring a box or some type container to carry your purchases.

name: Anything But a Brush at NPV

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: The natural world is full of unique shapes, patterns, and textures. Join Nature Center staff on a walk around the preserve to notice and collect loose natural materials. After our walk, we will return to the Nature Center to create art-the only rule is no paintbrushes! We will use our natural materials to create a unique work of art that celebrates the preserve. Come roll, press, swipe, and stamp with us!

name: AARP Smart Driver Course

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Co-sponsored by the AARP and Naperville Park District, this program (formerly known as the AARP Driver Safety Program) is a comprehensive driver-retraining course geared to the specific needs of older motorists. Learn the effects of aging and medications on driving, basic driving rules, license renewal procedures, local traffic hazards and more. Designed to improve your driving abilities through additional training, attention and practice, this two-day course helps you drive more safely and keep your driver's license longer. Most auto insurance companies offer a discount for people who attend this class. Call your local insurance agent for more details. The fee is $25 ($20 for AARP card-carrying members). Fees are subject to change. Payment goes directly to instructor. Make checks payable to AARP. Cash is not accepted. Although it is free to book a spot in the class, there is a fee for this program. (jg)

name: Adult Hike with a Naturalist

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

location: Street Parking on Feldott Lane or Violet Circle
description: Join a naturalist on a morning hike around the pond at Wildflower Park on Aurora Ave. The entire trail is paved and level. Bring a water bottle and wear sturdy walking shoes. Please note: Street Parking is on Feldott Lane or Violet Circle . A map showing these streets and the meeting location will be emailed to participants 3 days before the hike. No restrooms at this park. (ah)

name: Advanced Pottery and Sculpture

price.raw_price_text: Resident: $172.00; Non-resident: $202.00; Senior, 60 and over, resident: $137.60; Senior, 60 and over, non-resident: $161.60

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Challenge your hand-building and surface decorating skills in a relaxed studio atmosphere with individual guidance provided based on individual needs and requests. Class work explores unity of form and surface treatment with more complex forms using texture, color, scale and series of objects. Although the class title is "Advanced", only a beginning level of clay work and familiarity with the studio is required. Your inspiration may start with Pinterest, but you will leave the class with art that is uniquely yours. Bring your inspiration, sense of humor and desire to explore your creativity in an environment that fosters personal growth. Each participant receives an individual space to store work. All supplies are included. Prerequisite: participation in a previous Naperville Park District pottery class. No class June 29 & July 6. (bd)

name: Adventure Camp Grades: 1-5

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Adventure Camp is all about discovering new friendships, enjoying arts and crafts, playing lots of group games and participating in individual and team sports. On the first two Thursdays of the session, camp will travel to Centennial Beach and then on the last Thursday of the session, we'll take a field trip to a fun destination! On Thursdays, campers begin the day at 8:45 a.m. with pick up at 3:00 p.m. Campers need to bring a snack, drink and lunch each day. Fee includes Adventure Camp T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps (dn)

name: Adventures in Paleontology - Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: This is the perfect camp for the younger dinosaur lovers of the world. Each day we'll examine different types of authentic, prehistoric fossils and dinosaur bones, including Triceratops and T-Rex. Come and see the discoveries T-Rexplorers made at our 2025 digs, play some games, make some crafts and enjoy a variety of activities! Kids love this adventure and learn as they are having fun! Please bring a water bottle and healthy snack. We will be outdoors, so dress accordingly. (bd)

name: Adventures in Paleontology - Ultimate

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: This is as close as you can get to a dinosaur dig without leaving the state! Kids love this fun and adventurous "straight from the cretaceous period" camp because of its unique, hands-on exploration of dinosaur science and paleontology. Prepare to get dirty as we use the tools and skills utilized at a dig site. Each day we'll examine different types of authentic prehistoric fossils and dinosaur bones, including Triceratops and T-Rex. Come and see the discoveries T-Rexplorers made at our 2025 digs, play some games, make some crafts and enjoy a variety of activities! There's an explorer in all of us and if you're ready for an expedition in dinosaur discovery, this camp is for you! We will be outdoors so dress accordingly. Please bring a water bottle and healthy snack. (bd)

name: Ageless Grace®: Timeless Fit for the Body and Mind

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Welcome to Ageless Grace®: Timeless Fit for the Body and Mind, a cutting-edge brain fitness program based on neuroplasticity that activates all five functions of the brain-strategic planning, memory/recall, analytical thinking, creativity and imagination and kinesthetic learning while simultaneously addressing all 21 physical skills needed for lifelong optimal function. This unique program works for all ages and all fitness and ability levels. Instructor Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers will teach you the 21 Tools that focus on different anti-aging techniques like Shake It Up Baby, Dance Party, Spaghetti Spine and more, all set to lively and familiar music. Just imagine all of this plus tons of laughter. Stretch, bend and strengthen your core muscles while adding the twist of cognitive learning to build those brain cells. This program works by providing increased stability while seated in a chair! It's time to add fun to exercise and experience the newest way to move both mind and body. Please note that this class is done barefoot while sitting in a chair. Bring comfy socks if needed. (jg)

name: All-City Summer Series Pickleball Tournament

age_range.raw_age_text: 10 yrs +

description: This summer the Naperville Park District will launch the first ever pickleball tournaments. Beginner - this level includes pickleball players with a rating of 3.0 and below. These players have a very basic understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have some basic shots (such as a serve, return, medium paced drive, and dinks), but have limited consistency and control. Intermediate - this level of play would generally include pickleball players with a rating of 3.5-4.0. These players have a good understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have both forehand and backhand shots (including drop shots, backhand shots, and volleys), which are generally consistent with a moderate number of unforced errors. Advanced - this level is for players with a rating of 4.5 and above. These players have a strong understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have a great command over all shots on the pickleball court, with a limited number of unforced errors. (ba)

name: All-Star Baseball Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Kids learn the importance of proper throwing mechanics, rotational hitting, bunting, fielding, pitching and catching. Speed and agility techniques are added to increase core strength and mobility for added bat speed, range in the field and linear speed for base running. In-game strategies are included to increase each player's overall knowledge. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Basketball Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Fun basketball-like games are played to teach the importance of each skill learned.The foundation technique focuses on basic mechanics to build confidence and then adds larger challenges. Footwork is an extremely important aspect of the game; no player sits! We also work on dribbling with each hand, passing and shooting and understanding basic offense and defense in addition to learning teamwork and sportsmanship. Taught by All Star Sports. (sa)

name: All-Star Basketball Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Trainers focus on individual skills as well as team play. Each class begins with speed and agility drills to enhance each player's ability to get up and down the court quickly, generate rapid change of direction and create explosion to the basket. Ball handling, proper shooting technique, footwork and defensive/offensive strategies also are included. Small-sided competitions and game play enable each player to focus and work on skills learned. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Parent-Tot Sports

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 5 yrs

Program offers a great opportunity to improve the simple motor skills of catching, throwing, batting, shooting, passing, running and also improve developing hand-eye coordination. Parents participate with the child playing soccer, basketball, hockey, T-Ball, football and other sports. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Soccer Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Keep kids active and engaged both mentally and physically in this great base to prepare them for the next level of play. Soccer is a game that is action-packed so there's no sitting and waiting! The game of soccer is learned by hiding drills in fun games and using association techniques. Simple foot skills, dribbling, passing, shooting, basic rules and even work on spreading the field are covered. Kids also learn teamwork and sportsmanship. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Soccer Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: This program includes speed and agility drills to improve each player's soccer game by allowing for a more powerful shot, increased range on the field and efficient change of direction. Basic skills of dribbling, shooting passing and spacing are covered and expanded upon. Players learn the importance of movement away from the ball and the importance of each position through game situations. Taught by All Stars Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star Super Sports Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 5 yrs

description: Designed for the all-around athlete or the child who wants to take a shot at different sports. Kids stay active and work on balance, motor skills and hand-eye coordination while learning the rules of baseball, football, floor hockey, soccer, basketball and more! Each class focuses on a new sport, basic rules and mechanics while games are played that keep everyone moving. Led by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: All-Star T-Ball Juniors

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: T-Ball can be a boring game if taught incorrectly. This approach to baseball is one that engages players regardless of skill level. They learn basic building blocks in a fun, safe environment. Program keeps players moving and learning even while in the dugout! Mechanics and hand-eye coordination are the keys to early success. Players gain confidence as they learn the proper mechanics of catching, throwing, fielding, base-running and batting. This fun, exciting program prepares each player for the Level II, T-Ball or Coach Pitch leagues. Taught by All Star Sports Instruction, Inc. (sa)

name: Aquatic Fitness

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Tone muscles and increase cardiovascular fitness through various exercises while using the natural resistance and buoyancy of water. Swimming ability is not required. Ann Jansen will be the instructor for this class. For weather-related cancellations, please visit www.napervilleparks.org. (cj)

name: Archery

age_range.raw_age_text: 9 yrs +

description: Expert instruction in this Olympic sport is provided by a team of National Archery Association-certified instructors who teach target archery in a fun and safe environment. All instruction follows the Junior Olympic Archery Development program guidelines of the NAA. Tight-fitting clothing or short-sleeved shirts are recommended. All equipment is provided; please do not bring or buy any gear. Fee is per person. (fg)

name: Art Antics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3y 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: From 3D art to unconventional mediums, this camp is all about creativity and tapping into the artist's imagination! Each day will bring new, fun ways to create works of art in a variety of ways, challenging developing minds while providing opportunities to develop hands-on skills. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Baby Rock

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3m but less than 1 yr

description: Wiggle and giggle with Baby Rock! This program is a unique combination of sensory experiences with stimulating music and exercises to help strengthen and stretch your baby. Activities will include sing-alongs, exposure to simple instruments and sensory props, bean bag massages, motion exercises, bubbles, and more! Please bring a blanket or mat and get ready for a rockin' good time with your tiniest dancer! (sl)

name: Babysitter Training

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 17 yrs

description: The American Red Cross Babysitter’s Training with Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED - BL course prepares youth ages 11-16 to care for children and infants safely and confidently. It includes hands-on activities videos and discussions to develop essential real-life readiness babysitting skills. The course covers feeding, diapering, picking up and holding children safety and emergency response. We want to prepare participants well for emergencies but CPR can be physically demanding and participants should ideally weigh at least 85-90 pounds to participate. The First Aid/CPR/AED Blended Learning course includes an online portion and an instructor-led classroom skill session. The online portion must be completed prior to attending the in-person training and must be taken on a PC or tablet with a high-speed Internet connection. Allow approximately 3 hours to complete the online portion. The in-person portion of class will take 5 hours and 30 minutes. Upon successful completion of both the online and in person portions of the course a valid 10-year Babysitter's Training digital certification and a valid 2-year digital certificate for Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED is issued. (dn)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Get ready for an exciting five-day camp adventure where children meet and befriend summer gnomes and their cozy woodland homes. They will get to sculpt and design their own unique gnome characters using air-dry clay. These adorable creations will be built in their own miniature summer woodland worlds, filled with forest animals, mushrooms, flowers, and trees. Once a piece is done, the finishing touches with vibrant acrylic paints, a gloss sealer, and special paint pens can be applied. Each participant will get a personalized storage box to proudly display their work. All the clay, decorations, and art supplies will be provided, and they’ll be safe and non-toxic. To make sure projects come home safely, please bring a shoebox-sized box and an old kitchen towel by the end of the second day of class. (bd)

name: Deep Water Test Prep

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Classes are designed to help students pass the Centennial Beach deep water test. To pass the Centennial Beach deep water test students must be able to swim 100 meters of freestyle without stopping and with continuous proper form. Participants will build on their foundational knowledge of freestyle. Class size is generally a maximum of 5 students per instructor. The Centennial Beach Deep Water Swim test is offered at 12:50 pm, 2:50 pm and 5:50 pm daily in the lap lanes. Once the swimmer has successfully passed the test during the current season, they are issued a wristband at the Beach each time they visit. The wristband must be worn at all times during their visit so they are identified as a swimmer who can use the deep end. (cj)

name: Dementia-Friendly Movie Musicals

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Made for dementia participants and their family members/caregivers, enjoy movie musicals from the '20s to the '80s in the comfortably decorated lounge with movie theatre seats. Bring back fond memories while reminiscing about times that made you laugh and smile. The run time for each movie varies, but each shouldn't last more than two hours and fifteen minutes. Although this program is free, registration is required. This is a per person event; every dementia participant and family member/caregiver must register. (jg)

name: Digging Dinosaurs

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Journey to the prehistoric land of dinosaurs. This camp incorporates arts, crafts, games and stories to teach pint-sized paleontologists about these amazing extinct creatures. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Elan Family Picnic

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Pack your favorite picnic essentials and join us as we celebrate another successful season at the Élan Family Picnic! The event will be held at the Riverwalk Grand Pavilion, with parking available in the Centennial Beach parking lot on Jackson. The Riverwalk Grand Pavilion is located at the far end of the lot. Families are welcome to arrive between 4:00–4:30 PM, with the program beginning promptly at 4:30 PM. We’ll start with brief acknowledgements, followed by time to eat, connect, and reflect on highlights from the season. A few helpful notes: families are expected to bring their own picnic supplies and desired food, restrooms are available on site, and the space includes both covered picnic tables and an open grassy area for blankets. This is an outdoor event, so please come prepared to enjoy the weather. Please note: this event is reserved exclusively for Élan dancers and their families.(sl)

name: Elements of Art Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Enjoy summer art fun and more artistic discoveries! Participants are introduced to the elements of art: line, shape, color, texture, form, space, and value and become immersed in hands-on art using a variety of mediums to explore creative expression, leading to personal artistic discoveries. Supply fee of $20 is payable to the instructor at the first day of class. Participants may bring a snack and drink. (bd)

name: Elements of Art for Kids

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: Learn about the elements of art to create fun, one-of-a-kind creations with mosaics, mobiles, self-portraits & black and white pottery! Supply fee of $10 is payable to the instructor at the first day of class. (bd)

name: Elements of Art for Kids

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Learn about the three elements of art - line, shape and color - while creating fun, one-of-a-kind creations! Supply fee of $10 is payable to the instructor at the first class. (bd)

name: End of Summer Luau Glam Night

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Come join Glitzy Girlz staff and head to Hawaii before school starts! Our staff will be glamming up participants with hair flower, make-up sparkle and pretty nail polish application complete with flower nail stickers. They will decorate a craft with paints, stencils and flower embellishments and jewels. They will also design a fun beaded bracelet with Hawaiian charms. Each participant will receive a take home outfit of a flower lei and a flowered Hawaiian skirt for photos at our palm tree backdrop and props. The class ends with maraca freeze dance and limbo line! Come vacay with friends! This is a drop-off independent class; parents do not stay. (bd)

name: Fairy Tale Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: For kids who love the world of make-believe, this storybook-themed camp is the perfect opportunity to let them live out their magical fantasy through stories, games, and role play. Think princesses, knights, dragons, castles and quests! Come dressed as your favorite prince, princess or storybook character! Please no "princess" shoes or flip-flops. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Fall Baseball

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Play ball! Young athletes begin learning the game of baseball with an introduction to the basic skills of hitting, catching, throwing and base-running. The first two weeks will consist of Saturday practice and for the last five weeks, we will play games on Sunday afternoon. Each player will receive a MLB replica hat! Two adult volunteer coaches are needed for each team. Both team and individual registration is available. Each team has a maximum of 12 players. Registration CLOSES on August 12, 2025 at 11:59 pm (fg)

name: Fall Naperville Premier Soccer League Interest List

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Individual players that would like to play in the NPSL but don't have a team, may add themselves to the interest list. Coaches looking for additional players are provided with the parent contact information and the coach will contact parents directly to discuss team information. Placement is not guaranteed . This is NOT a registration for the program.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

name: Family Hike with a Naturalist

age_range.raw_age_text: 3 yrs +

description: Join a naturalist on an early morning hike to learn about the animals and plants that call Knoch Knolls Park home. The route is mostly over grassy or gravel paths. Please register only one member of your family. No pets please. Bring a water bottle and wear sturdy walking shoes. Meets on the nature center deck. (ah)

name: Fencing Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Enjoy five days of fencing fun! Fencing is a recreational and competitive sport that incorporates agility, strength, coordination, balance and timing. This camp provides foil-based instruction. Instructor Peter Habala is a five-time National Champion from Romania with over 25 years of fencing experience and the head coach at RedStar Fencing Chicago. (fg)

name: Fencing: Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Fencing is a recreational and competitive sport that incorporates agility, strength, coordination, balance and timing. This program focuses on the discipline and training in foil. A foil is a thrusting weapon with a thin, flexible blade and a small, round bell guard. This program runs concurrently in the same room as the club program with adults and children fencing together. Equipment is provided. (fg)

name: Fencing: Youth

age_range.raw_age_text: 10 yrs +

description: Fencing is a recreational and competitive sport that incorporates agility, strength, coordination, balance and timing. This program focuses on the discipline and training in foil. A foil is a thrusting weapon with a thin, flexible blade and a small, round bell guard. Equipment is provided for beginning and intermediate participants; participants enrolled in Club Fencing should purchase their own electric equipment. Participants must have completed beginning fencing and have instructor approval before signing up for intermediate fencing and instructor approval to sign up for Club Fencing. (fg)

name: Fishin' Kids

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12 yrs

location: May Watt Park; Meets at entrance on Oakton Lane
description: Learn all the basics of fishing including how to rig a pole, bait the hook, cast and handle fish. Parent must remain with their child(ren) during the class. Bring folding lawn chairs. All fishing poles, bait and tackle are provided. We'll be fishing rain or shine (but not if it's thundering - check our Rainout Line ), so please dress for the weather. Fishing takes place at May Watts Park's pond and meets at entrance on Oakton Lane. Price is per child; at least one adult must attend with each family. (ah)

name: Fort Hill Open Gymnastics Waiver

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Fort Hill Gymnastics Open Gym - Come experience the Fort Hill Gymnastics facility as a family! This registration is only to complete your waiver. Admission fee will be charged per visit. Instruction not provided during open gym. Parents and Guardians are free Children ages 6 to 11 must have an adult in the Fort Hill building during open gym. Children under 11 must be walked to the gymnastics room and picked up from the gymnastics supervisor at the end of open gym. Children ages 4 - 5 must be within arm's reach of an adult in the gymnastics room. Open Gymnastics is from 2:30pm-4:00pm during the months of January, February, March, April, May, September, October, November, and December. Open Gymnastics from Saturday, June 13 to Saturday, July 25 is from 12:30pm-2:00pm. There is no Open Gymnastics on the following dates: April 4, April 18, May 2, May 16, May 23, May 30, June 6, July 4, August 1-September 5, October 31, December 19, December 26.

name: Free Outdoor Fitness and Wellness Events

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

name: Fun With Flags Camp! Color Guard Performance Skills

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Designed for students ages 7-17 with some basic color guard flag experience, this four-day camp will enhance the skills of performers of all levels. If you are a young performer getting ready for your next performance season or a high school student who wants to learn a new piece of equipment, this camp is for you! Staff from the Park District Steperettes program will be assisted by members from DCI World Class color guards. Frequent regrouping of participants based on skills development will lead to performance growth. Class will run Monday-Wednesday 8:30 - 11:30 am and 8:30 - 1 pm on Thursday with a performance for families at noon. Please bring snacks and beverages and color guard equipment. (fg)

name: Fun with Flags!

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Learn to spin and toss a flag while moving to music - just like they do in parades and at football games! Enroll in the Beginner level if you are just starting. The Intermediate class instruction will be differentiated according to ability level and usually includes small equipment spinning. Students will perform a routine for their family and friends at the last class session. Equipment is provided by the program, but new flags are available for purchase for $33 from the instructor. (fg)

name: Golf Lessons: Adult Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Our PGA professionals offer instructional clinics catering to beginning golfers that include instruction on full swing, pitching, chipping, putting, rules and etiquette. Receive a lesson guide and a four-token range punch card - a $60 value. The first and second lessons are scheduled for two hours; the third and fourth lessons are scheduled for one hour. Participants should provide their own clubs. A driver or fairway wood, the 7, 9, Pw or Sw irons, and a putter are recommended. If you do not have clubs, we have golf clubs available for use at no charge. Participants also are eligible for a discount on club purchases in our Golf Shops. For rainout information, call the Springbrook Golf Shop at 630-848-5060 or the Naperbrook Golf Shop at 630-378-4215. (ml, jw)

name: Golf Lessons: Adult Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Our PGA professionals offer instructional clinics catering to beginning golfers that include instruction on full swing, pitching, chipping, putting, rules and etiquette. Receive a lesson guide and a four-token range punch card - a $60 value. The first and second lessons are scheduled for two hours; the third and fourth lessons are scheduled for one hour. Please provide your own clubs. A fairway wood, the 5, 7, 9 irons and a putter are recommended. If you cannot provide your own clubs, please contact the course where lessons are scheduled so we can accommodate you. You also are eligible for a discount on club purchases in our Golf Shops. For rainout information, call the Naperbrook Golf Shop at 630-378-4215.

name: Golf Lessons: Playing Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Our PGA professionals offer instructional clinics (four hours range time/four hours course time) designed for golfers seeking to improve their playing ability. Instruction on full swing, pitching, chipping, putting, rules and etiquette and basic golf course management playing skills is provided. To make this program enjoyable for all participants, golfers should have some on-course playing experience. Receive a lesson guide and a four-token range punch card - a $60 value. Participants should provide their own clubs. A full set of clubs is recommended. We do have golf club sets available at no charge. Participants also are eligible for a discount on club purchases in our Golf Shops. For rainout information, call the Springbrook Golf Shop at 630-848-5060 or the Naperbrook Golf Shop at 630-378-4215. (ml)

name: Good Times Day Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Good Times Day Camp is the perfect choice for families looking for the district's popular full day camp activities but want access to an indoor location throughout the day. This full-day, week-long camp keeps kids having fun all summer! They'll discover new friendships, enjoy arts and crafts, play group games and participate in individual and team sports. Camp will travel to Centennial Beach twice a week to swim and take a field trip to a fun destination once each week. Campers need to bring their lunch each day except Thursday when a pizza, chips and lemonade lunch is provided. Fee includes Good Times Day Camp T-shirt to wear on field trip days. Early pickup is available at 3:00 p.m. each day except Friday field trip days. Registration numbers for day camps are closed on the Wednesday of the week prior to camp. Registrations for day camps are accepted only up to a determined maximum number. Closing of registrations for day camp is being implemented in order for the Park District to monitor camp enrollment and ensure proper staffing levels. All detailed information about camp is located at www.napervilleparks.org/camps. (dn)

name: Guitar Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: 6 yrs +

description: Learn with efficiency and confidence by a trained and experienced coach. Group lessons offer the right environment and community to nurture your focus and motivation. Bring your own guitar; rentals can be arranged by calling 630-717-0562. A $15 fee for the required lesson book is paid to the instructor at the first class. (sl)

name: Guitar Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

name: Gym Cats Camp: Summer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6y 1m

description: Calling all mini-gymnasts! Experience our Gym Tigers program in a whole new way! This camp is a fun way to learn the basics of gymnastics on bars, beams, vaults and floor equipment. Campers will be grouped by age/skill level to ensure a quality learning experience. Please bring a water bottle to each class. Parents will be able to view each class, in our new Fort Hill Activity Center. (dn)

name: Gym Cats: Session I

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1 yr but less than 7 yrs

description: Budding gymnasts love this exciting prelude to gymnastics! The program provides work on bars, vault, beam and floor at all age levels. Gymnasts work the Tumbl Trak or pit each week. Gymnasts remain with their age group until they are old enough to qualify in the next age group. Coaches notify you when your gymnast has achieved the skills they need to move up to a Level 2 program. They reserve the right to move your child into an appropriate program if they believe placement is incorrect. Children participating without an adult must be toilet-trained. (dn)

name: Gymnastics Camp: Summer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Learn and develop new gymnastics skills including vault, balance beam, floor and bars. Tumbling Camp will only work on skills for floor exercise. Enjoy a variety of games and meet new friends. All experience levels are welcome; campers will be grouped by skill level. Please bring water each day. Parents will be able to view each class in our new Fort Hill Activity Center

name: Gymnastics: Levels 1-5 Session I

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Student gymnasts learn skills pertaining to floor, beam, bars and vault. They focus on building strength, body awareness and hand-eye coordination through repetition of weekly drills and the instruction that is essential to fully develop skills. Each level builds on the previous level with instructor approval and certain skill achievement necessary to move up. Your gymnast should expect to be in a level for a year before advancing. Coaches reserve the right to move the gymnast to the appropriate program if they believe placement is incorrect. Gymnasts must be 6 years old by September 1, 2026, to begin this program. (dn)

name: Gymnastics: Tumbling Levels 1-2 Session I

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Tumbling develops coordination, strength, balance and self-confidence. Level 1 is for children who are new to tumbling. Form and positions will be taught at this level in addition to forward and backward roll, straddle roll, dive roll, lunge to handstand, cartwheel and bridge. Class is commonly repeated before the instructor recommends moving up to Tumbling 2. Tumbling 2 students will learn handstand forward roll, front limber, back walkover and round off. Instructors reserve the right to move students to appropriate levels. Children must be 6 years old by September 1, 2026 to be in this program. (dn)

name: Hip Hop/Jazz Fusion

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Filled with great music and good times, this program provides a structured method of learning various hip-hop and jazz dance moves in a fun-filled, vibrant environment. It focuses on age-appropriate dance steps and music. Kids love combining street dance with funk and jazz, similar to what they see in televised dance performances or music videos. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

description: This course will teach children/tweens how to be safe at home. Topics covered include Fire Prevention, Water, Internet, Stranger and Electrical Safety. (dn)

name: Horsemanship Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Horse enthusiasts love this camp that gives them the opportunity to ride! Campers also learn about horse grooming and general care through hands-on experience. Riders must bring a bicycle or riding helmet. All riders must wear long pants, a T-shirt or sweatshirt and closed toe shoes (preferably gym shoes). Due to a weight restriction, all riders must be 150 pounds or less. All instruction is indoors. Parent must sign an additional waiver. Call 630-844-3533 with questions. (dn)

name: How Taxes Impact Retirement Income

age_range.raw_age_text: 40 yrs +

description: If you are nearing retirement or already retired, you need to understand how taxes impact your retirement income, as it may be possible to pay less in taxes on your hard-earned dollars. Learn the most up-to-date and comprehensive information regarding retirement taxation, including ways to efficiently harvest income sources, whether they are Social Security, 401K/IRA, other sources or a combination of them all. Presentation provided by Greg Kurinec. Although this program is free, registration is required. (jg)

description: Our Staff Coaches at All Seasons Ice Rinks make learning to skate fun & safe for people of all ages & abilities. We follow the curriculum designed by Learn To Skate USA; each level builds upon the skills already mastered. We suggest wearing helmets, gloves/mittens, athletic-like pants, and a warm jacket. We offer skate rental for $28 per session or $4 weekly. Free practice times for all class times and one makeup allowed per session. Please call 630-851-0755 or visit www.allseasonsicerinks.com for questions or additional information. (dn)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: The goal at Rocket Ice Arena is to provide a fun and safe environment for skaters to learn to skate and to be able to continue on in hockey or figure skating. From tot and up, lessons are presented in concise levels with each one focusing on skills that will serve as building blocks for future levels. After demonstrating mastery in one level, the student skater may proceed to the next. The curriculum works in conjunction with USFS Basic Skills Program that is taught in quality rinks worldwide. Please wear athletic pants and fleece jacket or similar fitted and warm jacket and bring gloves. Helmets are recommended. We have skates available to rent. Please call 630-679-1700 or visit Rocketice.com if you have any questions. (dn)

name: Jazz: Level 2/3

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Dancers build technique and begin to use strengthening exercises to build stamina and increase their knowledge of jazz footwork and style. ***Prerequisite of the previous level or equivalent experience is required. For questions on placement, please contact the Dance Coordinator at tlight@napervilleparks.org or 630-848-3618*** Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. name: Jr. 9 Hole League

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 17 yrs

description: The Junior 9-Hole League is designed for golfers with some on-course playing experience. Participants play 9-holes and receive lunch each week in addition to a four-token range punch card - a $40 value. Knowledge of some basic rules and etiquette is helpful but not required. Participants are screened for skill level the first week. Those who do not meet the program requirements will be given a full refund. We require each participant to have their own set of clubs. We have a limited number of junior golf clubs available at no charge that can be reserved on a first come, first served basis by contacting the Golf Shop where the league is held. Participants are also eligible for advantage pricing on club purchases. (ml, dh)

Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc) Stem: Join us as we explore engineering by building towers, bridges, catapults, marble coasters and more! Ocean: Ever wonder how whales stay warm or why beaches erode or how light dictates what lives in the layers of the ocean? Join us as we explore the wonders of the ocean! Space: Suit up and blast into space! Learn about astronauts and explore the galaxy. Cooking: Edible science week where children can really eat their science experiments. Water & Ice: This week, we will be exploring the properties of water through fun, hands-on activities. Chemistry: This week is all about chemical reactions, osmosis, emulsification and more! Physics: This week, we will be exploring matter, surface tension, buoyancy and more! Insects: Buzz, crawl, and flutter into a week of insect discovery! Preschool campers will study butterflies, ants, bees, ladybugs, and more through sensory play, storytelling, science experiments, and creative art projects.

name: Magic Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Step into a world of illusion and imagination at Magic Camp! Campers will learn awe-inspiring tricks, sleight of hand, and performance skills from an experienced, local magician. From mastering card tricks and mind-reading to grand illusions, every child will build confidence, creativity, and showmanship. Plus, campers will receive a variety of magic props to take home, so the fun doesn’t have to end when camp does! The week concludes with a special magic show where campers dazzle their families with their new skills! (bd)

name: Magical Creatures

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3y 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Bring your imagination to this camp as we explore magical creatures from unicorns to dragons. These mythical and fantastic creatures will inspire our art, activities and games in this creatively themed program. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Mandala Art/Dot Painting Class

age_range.raw_age_text: 12 yrs +

description: Mandala Art was originated in India. From there, it spread all over the world; it is sometimes referred to as "dot painting." In this class, participants will learn how to create their own piece of art on an 8"x8" canvas, using their own inspiration and ideas. During the first 20 minutes of the class, participants will receive step-by-step guidance on how to create their own masterpiece by using specific dot painting tools. All tools and paints provided. Participants will be able to choose what colors they wish to work with as well. No artistic background is required. Participants also will receive a free tote bag and a light snack. If you would like more information on Mandala Art, please contact Vanessa at vvvdow@hotmail.com. Vanessa can share photos and provide more information on the class. (bd)

name: Martial Arts: ISKC Karate Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Illinois Shotokan Karate Club (ISKC) is Chicagoland's premier karate school taught under the instruction of john DiPasquale, a four-time nation Champion, US National Coach and President of the US National Karate Federation. The adult program releases tension, develops total body fitness and builds stamina and overall productivity! In addition to self-defense skills, karate increases flexibility, cardiovascular endurance and muscle tone while improving core strength. (fg) Uniforms and Belt-Testing are options available through the ISKC instructor. Youth, Parent/Child and Adult Classes may train together. Beginner students are not permitted to register for the current session after the second class has met. Registration for continuers through the advanced students is accepted after the start date, but payment of the full fee is required.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: This progressive martial arts program teaches the basics in karate, self-defense, sparring, kata and children's safety with belt progression through Black Belt. name: Martial Arts: Kids Kung Fu

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: The focus in all levels is on building character and personal achievement and not in aggression and competition. Students earn increasingly higher belts as they progress in knowledge and abilities. Information regarding additional costs for T-shirts required for Level 2 & 3 will be discussed at first class and will be purchased directly through instructor. (jg) Level 1 - Students begin with simple exercises and routines that develop confidence and self-discipline as well as build coordination and strength. Level 2 - Students proceed through more difficult routines that demand a higher level of focus and concentration. Two-person Kung Fu practice is introduced that allows the students to develop their skills together. Instructor approval is required. Level 3 - This level is for those students that are on the road to their Kung Fu Black Belt. Training in child-appropriate staff and sword is introduced along with child-appropriate martial arts applications. Instructor approval is required.
