name: Mean Girls

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Paramount Theatre, Aurora This hilarious musical has heart, telling the story of Cady Heron, a sweet and smart new girl who has just moved from Africa to suburban Illinois. When she enters the wild world of North Shore High, she quickly finds herself tangled up with The Plastics, the school's most popular and most ruthless clique led by queen bee Regina George. As Cady tries to fit in, she learns that popularity comes with a price, and revenge can get ugly fast. Seats are on the main floor. Lunch includes hot entree, potato or rice, vegetable, rolls, dessert and beverage. Price includes transportation, lunch and theatre ticket. (jg)

name: Meditation for Youth

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: This program is much more than just a basic class on calming the body and mind. Participants will learn the tools needed for managing a multitude of concerns including stress, anxiety, emotions, family togetherness, and more. As they progress from youth and adolescence, participants will benefit from understanding the importance of mindfulness and coping skills. Jitendra Desai employs the right method for teaching and helping students tap into the proper ways of handling difficult situations that arise. (km)

name: Mini Music Makers

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Make music with your little one! Join local music school, Edge Music Academy, for an early childhood music class led by a licensed, board-certified music therapist. This is a sing-along experience with percussion instruments and other fun accessories, perfect for young children to explore music in an intimate, hands-on setting. A parent or caregiver must be present for all class times due to the young age of students. (sl)

name: Modern/Contemporary: Adult Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Learn the fundamentals of modern/contemporary dance while strengthening and toning your body and increasing your flexibility. This program is perfect for students new to the modern/contemporary style of dance or those looking to return to the art. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Mudrats Swim Team

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Children through young adults are invited to join the Mudrats Swim Team to enhance competitive strokes, conditioning, starts, turns and more. Mudrats swimmers are highly encouraged to participate in meets, have fun, and do their best regardless of whether they win or lose. Prerequisites: Swimmers must meet the stated age requirement by May 31, 2026. Swimmers eight years and under should be able to swim freestyle and backstroke for 25 yards. Swimmers nine years and older should be able to swim freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly for 50 yards. Parental Requirements: Parents, or other family members, must work a designated number of volunteer jobs at meets and/or Mudrat activities during the season (plus City Meet and/or Classic Meet). Swimmers will not be eligible to declare for meets without meeting the designated number of jobs per family. The Mudrats Parent Board will assess a fine for each missed job; multiple missed jobs may result in swimmer ineligibility to attend meets, practices, or social events. Two or three meets are scheduled weekly from mid-June through July and will be held on Tuesday or Thursday evenings or Saturday mornings. No refunds will be given after the first week of practice. A new parent meeting and open house will be scheduled before the start of the season. Practices will be held in the evening at an indoor location the first two weeks of practice. Information for practice times and location for the first week will be available on the Mudrat's web site. (jg)

name: Music for Little Mozarts

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: This class is designed to give your child an exciting introduction to more formal piano instruction. Students will learn musical concepts as they relate to the keyboard while developing singing, movement, and listening skills simultaneously with an introduction to musical styles. A colorful workbook is in included. (sl)

name: Music for Little Mozarts

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: This class is designed to give your child an exciting introduction to more formal piano instruction. Students will learn musical concepts as they relate to the keyboard while developing singing, movement, and listening skills simultaneously with an introduction to musical styles. The required lesson and workbooks are available from the instructor at the first class for $15. (sl)

name: Music Makers Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Love to move and grove? This camp is for you! Sing, dance and make musical instruments. Campers must be toilet-trained and be able to separate from parent/caregiver. Please, no flip-flops. If your child has allergies or asthma that require an Epi-pen or inhaler to accompany your child, please contact Sara Cass at scass@napervilleparks.org to complete the necessary paperwork at least 5 days before the start of camp. (sc)

name: Musical Theater Dance: Junior

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Do you dream of being on Broadway someday? In this class dancers will learn about the art of musical theater as they combine acting and dancing to create a spectacular performance. Each class focuses on dance technique, acting, and team building. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Musical Theater Dance: Level 1

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Do you dream of being on Broadway someday? In this class dancers will learn about the art of musical theater as they combine singing, acting and dancing to create a spectacular performance. Each class focuses on dance technique, acting, singing skills and team building. It is perfect for someone new to musical theater and dance or a seasoned performer looking enhance their skills. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: MusiCreators: Nature's Music

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1 yr but less than 6 yrs

description: In a world filled with "be alone" activities, spend more one-on-one, fun-filled, quality and engaging time together. In this MusiCreators program with a Musikgarten curriculum, participate in fun and developmentally appropriate activities that stimulate imagination and improve increasing vocabulary. Children gain independence, confidence and learn self-expression through singing songs. They'll play and enjoy lots of movement while improving their gross and fine motor coordination. Each session is filled with new songs, new activities and many wonderful instruments. (sl)

name: Naperville Premier Soccer League University-1st Grade

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: The Naperville Premier Soccer League University is an opportunity for 1st grade teams to receive specialized training, while still cultivating a recreational experience. Teams receive one training session per week with a certified soccer trainer, and have games with their volunteer coach on Saturdays. This is a recreational program, no scores or standings are kept. Games are played against NYS teams and must follow the NYS policies such as no running-up of scores. Referees will not be utilized; teams will use parent volunteers and coaches as referees and linesmen. Players must wear the NYS reversible jersey. Non-residents are charged an additional $20 per player which is collected during the roster process. A $200 non-refundable deposit with auto-draw payment plan set-up or full payment is due at the time of registration. The last day to register or withdraw and receive a refund minus the $200 deposit is June 16. There are 7 games in the season and 9 weeks of training. Practices begin the week of August 25 and the first game is September 12. For additional information, please contact Susan Wasson at swasson@napervilleparks.org or www.napervilleparks.org/napervillepremiersoccerleague. (sa)

name: Naperville Premier Soccer League: 2nd Boys

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: The Naperville Premier Soccer League is designed for teams seeking a program with an enhanced focused on player development and increased competition – still within a recreational environment. Optional technical and tactical training is provided weekly by a certified soccer trainer. Practice time and location is determined by the team and is based on trainer availability. There are 7 games in the season that take place on Saturdays at various parks in Naperville. Non-residents are charged an additional $20 per player which is collected during the roster process. The last day to register for a trainer option is June 16. The last day to register for the league-only option is June 30. A $200 non-refundable deposit with auto-draw payment plan set-up or full payment is due at the time of registration. Teams registering for a “trainer option” have until June 16 to withdraw and receive a refund, minus the $200 deposit. After June 16, the training portion of the fee is non-refundable. Teams registering for “league-only” option have until June 30 to withdraw and receive a refund, minus the $200 deposit. After June 30 all fees are non-refundable. Practices start the week of August 25 with the first game scheduled for September 12. Teams are required to review the complete league details at www.napervilleparks.org/napervillepremiersoccerleague prior to registering. (sa)

name: Naperville Youth NFL FLAG Football

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: The Naperville Park District has partnered with the National Football League to offer this flag football league where players learn the game of football in a safe setting. Program emphasizes positive coaching and provides an environment where every child has the opportunity to succeed. Teams typically practice two nights weekly prior to the start of the game schedule and one night weekly once games begin. Practices take place between the hours of 4:00-7:00 p.m. for approximately 60-75 minutes. Participants play a seven-game schedule on Friday nights or Sunday afternoons beginning September 5. All games are played in Naperville at Commissioners Park, Nike Sports Complex, Knoch Park or Prairie Park. Volunteer parent coaches are needed . Players are contacted by their coach with the time of their practice during the week before the first practice. Each player receives an NFL team reversible jersey and an official NFL FLAG belt. Players must provide their own mouthguard. (ba)

name: Naperville Youth Soccer: Boys 1st Grade

description: Become a night owl and explore Knoch Knolls Park after dark! Learn about the local animals, like coyotes, owls, and raccoons and their amazing adaptations for a nocturnal lifestyle. Bring a healthy snack and water bottle each day. (ah)

name: Nature: Night Shift Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Become part of Knoch Knolls Park's night shift as you explore the woodlands, prairies and river. Discover the amazing adaptations that animals like fireflies, white-tailed deer, and opossums have for making a living at night. Bring a healthy snack and water bottle each day. (ah)

name: Nature: Outdoor Adventure Skills Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Spend time learning about, and practicing, outdoor skills like pitching a tent, fishing, campfire safety, reading maps, making S'mores and more. Collect and decorate your own walking stick to take home after camp. Bring a healthy snack and water bottle each day. (ah)

name: Nature: Prehistoric Pals Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Travel back in time to the age of the dinosaurs and the last ice age. Learn about different dinosaurs and giant dragonflies, our state fossil, the Tully Monster, and ice age animals like the woolly mammoth and saber-toothed cats! Bring a water bottle and healthy snack each day and wear clothes that can get wet and dirty. (ah)

name: New Horizons Band DuPage

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: New Horizons Band DuPage provides musical instrument instruction and music-making for active adults and seniors, including those with no previous musical experience and those who have been musically inactive. Learn how to read music and play a musical instrument, or jump right in and participate in a concert band (musical instrument experience required). Every person has musical potential that can be developed to a level that will be personally rewarding. Individuals are encouraged to practice on their own outside of class and may be invited to perform in concerts at the end of each season. Each participant must own, purchase, rent or borrow the band instrument that they choose to play. New Horizons Band DuPage has some instruments that can be rented or can suggest locations where instruments can be rented or purchased. Music method books are required for the beginner and intermediate classes. Payment of $10 will be collected at the first class (price subject to change). Please make checks payable to New Horizons Band. Visit www.nhbdupage.org for more information. It's never too late to toot your own horn! (jg)

name: Not Your Grandma's Art Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Spend a week with artist Charlie Heinrich / Art Wizard! In addition to having fun, students will use unexpected ideas and materials along with various concepts including line, form, color, shape to make art objects. We'll also try out different hands-on techniques like drawing, painting, sculpting, combining, constructing, gluing, hot gluing, cutting, sawing, sanding, drilling, tying, wiring, and thinking. Some of the topics we plan to cover are: aliens, flying saucers, airplanes, sail boats, birds, skulls, hearts, robots, super heroes, snakes, alligators, animals, people and wherever our imagination takes us. Parents, clear off your refrigerator and mantel, because your camper will be creating a lot of unique and fun art that you'll want to display. Participants should bring a lunch, snacks and something to drink. Supply fee of $40 is due to the instructor at the first class. (bd)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 4 yrs

description: The NYS Academy program is a great opportunity for younger children to become part of our Naperville Youth Soccer tradition. This coed, practice-only program introduces basic soccer skills in a fun, active and social environment. Teams meet once a week for approximately 30 - 45 minutes. Weekly practice locations and times are listed below. Please register according to your player’s age as of 9/1/2026. Please register or waitlist for one team only. Anyone registered on a team AND on a waitlist will be removed from the waitlist without notice. Adult volunteer coaches are required for each team. Players will be contacted by their coach the week of August 16. For more information, please visit https://napervilleparks.org/napervilleyouthsocceracademy. (sa)

name: Odyssey Lunch Cruise

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: Navy Pier, Chicago Delight in spending an afternoon of dining and sightseeing along the shores of Lake Michigan. While on board the Odyssey, enjoy listening, and even dancing, to a variety of music. Also enjoy an unbelievable three-course, gourmet lunch including choice of Grilled Peach and Arugula Salad or Roasted Red Pepper Bisque, main course choice of Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Smoked Chili-Rubbed Atlantic Salmon or Seasonal Potato Gnocchi and dessert choice of Spanish Basque Style Cheesecake, Chocolate Toffee Crunch Cake or Mixed Berries and Pineapple as well as a beverage (menu subject to change). Price includes transportation, cruise, music and lunch. (bn)

name: Outdoor: Beach Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Enjoy a relaxing and energizing yoga practice complete with the beautiful views of Centennial Beach. Bring a yoga mat and a beach towel and find joy as you spend time in the sand and grass overlooking the water. Leave feeling refreshed, focused, peaceful, grateful and strong. No previous yoga experience is required, only an open and positive attitude. (km)

name: Paddleboard Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Enjoy practicing your favorite yoga routines on the water! Strengthen your core while developing better balance and coordination. Each class culminates in relaxation leaving you feeling refreshed, focused, peaceful, grateful and strong. You must be comfortable in and around the water. Minimal yoga experience is helpful, but not required. Arrive dressed to enter the water. Led by encouraging and experienced yoga instructor, Ann Gasperec. (km)

name: Paddlewheel Riverboat & Durant-Peterson House

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: St. Charles, IL Start with a 1.5-hour private charter paddlewheel boat ride down a quiet and peaceful section of the Fox River. Learn about the history of the St. Charles area. Lunch on board will be served on the lower deck. Bagged lunch choices are a ham sub sandwich or turkey sub sandwich with chips, cookies and a drink. If you have dietary restrictions, please choose the applicable option during registration. Although there are nice views from the lower level and bow, head to the upper deck after lunch (12-15 steps) for a more expansive view. Visit the 1843 Durant-Peterson House museum. Docents dressed in period clothing will bring the group back in time to experience what life was like living on the Illinois Prairie in the late 1800s. Partake in an heirloom apple sampling. Learn the history of apples around the world and how apples became a vital part of pioneer life. There will be a variety of heirloom apples to taste and compare. Price includes transportation, lunch, boat ride, museum entrance with guide and apple tasting. (jg)

name: Parent/Child Dino Hour in the Park

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Bring your little one for an hour of dinosaur discovery fun! They'll see and touch real dinosaur fossils, listen to a story, make a craft to take home and dig in the sand to assemble dinosaur puzzle pieces. This is a parent/child activity. Register child only; parent attends for free. (bd)

name: Parking Permits

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 15 yrs but less than 20 yrs

description: The Naperville Park District offers parking spaces for Neuqua Valley and Naperville Central High School students. Permit holders will be eligible for parking in the designated spaces at the Skate Park lot at Frontier, the gravel lot off of West Street or the designated spaces at the Centennial Beach parking lot. Permits purchased online will be mailed to the address listed on your account within two weeks of purchase. If you purchase online, your receipt will act as your confirmation of purchase until your receive your permit. Please print your receipt and place it on your dashboard until your permit arrives. Permits also may be purchased in person at the Alfred Rubin Riverwalk Community Center, the Knoch Knolls Nature Center or the Fort Hill Activity Center. Applications must be signed by a parent or guardian. Spaces are not assigned and are available first come, first served ONLINE REGISTRATION OPENS JULY 12, 2025. WALK IN WILL BE AVAILABLE JULY 12, 2025. CHECK WEBSITE FOR FACILITY HOURS. If you are participating in your school lottery for a permit, please wait for those results before purchasing an NPD parking permit.

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

Program consists of instruction followed by actual game play. Players should wear athletic shoes and dress as for tennis. Equipment is provided, but bring your own Pickleball paddle if you have one. (ba)

name: Pickleball Tournament - 60+ Mixed Doubles (Intermediate)

age_range.raw_age_text: 60 yrs +

description: This summer the Naperville Park District will launch the first ever pickleball tournaments. Beginner - this level includes pickleball players with a rating of 3.0 and below. These players have a very basic understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have some basic shots (such as a serve, return, medium paced drive, and dinks), but have limited consistency and control. Intermediate - this level of play would generally include pickleball players with a rating of 3.5-4.0. These players have a good understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have both forehand and backhand shots (including drop shots, backhand shots, and volleys), which are generally consistent with a moderate number of unforced errors. Advanced - this level is for players with a rating of 4.5 and above. These players have a strong understanding of the rules and strategy of pickleball and have a great command over all shots on the pickleball court, with a limited number of unforced errors. (ba)

name: Pickleball: Practice with the Pro Private Instruction

age_range.raw_age_text: 4 yrs +

description: Our pickleball pros are available for private or semi-private lessons scheduled at a mutually-convenient time. Lessons with one of our Certified Pros are $79 per hour. Purchase a five-lesson package and save. To schedule a private lesson, register for the lesson and a staff member will be in touch with you to schedule the day and time. Lesson cancelations must be done 24 hours in advance in order to receive a credit. (ba)

Ballet shoes are optional for parent/caregiver. Adult is free and must accompany child; maximum two children per adult. Please register each child separately. name: Pottery

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The unique environment of a pottery studio is relaxing and conducive to creativity. Learn basic hand-building and surfacing techniques, the production stages of glazing and how to design and develop projects. All supplies are included. (bd)

description: Build castles, make coil pots or create a favorite animal - the possibilities are endless! Learn basic hand-building techniques and the stages of the glazing process. name: Pottery: Fairy House Building

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 13 yrs

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: This TRX/GRIT class is designed to build strength, stability, and endurance. Using the TRX suspension trainer, participants engage in controlled, bodyweight movements that enhance full‑body strength, balance, core stability, and mobility. GRIT incorporates high‑intensity interval exercises to elevate heart rate, improve muscular endurance, and boost overall athletic performance. This dynamic, results‑driven workout is suitable for all fitness levels, with modifications and progressive options to meet each participant where they are. Expect to be challenged safely and confidently as you work toward your personal fitness goals. Fort Hill Fitness members, contact the Fort Hill Activity Center at 630-995-8900 to register. (km)

name: Private Voice Lessons

age_range.raw_age_text: 5 yrs +

description: Develop your voice and learn performance skills! Lessons include breathing, technical exercises and warm-ups. Our expert instructors will help pick perfect songs for your voice and style. You will be contacted by The Music Suite to schedule your lessons. Classes are 30 minutes long and there are 7 classes in a session. (sl)

name: Red, White & Bingo Luncheon

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: This special patriotic edition of bingo features a festive luncheon, along with 12 games of regular bingo, great company, and if you’re lucky, exciting prizes. Enjoy a traditional American hot-dog lunch and plenty of red, white, and blue spirit as we celebrate 250 years of the USA together! (jg)

name: Regain Your Balance

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Taught by instructor Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers, Regain Your Balance is specifically designed for seniors who are currently mobile and able to support themselves without assistance. As seniors progress and notice a decline in cognitive function, the biggest fear is falling. Consisting of three 15-minute segments of sitting, standing and walking, this class will help you build your confidence and regain or maintain your balance. Fall prevention and how to correctly fall to avoid injuries will be discussed. Please bring water for hydration and wear gym shoes with good support. In order to participate in the Regain Your Balance class, you must be mobile and able to support yourself without assistance. (jg)

name: Rhythm Express: Family Music Time

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9m but less than 7 yrs

description: Enjoy musical fun for your whole family! Experience singing, creative movement, family jam sessions and fun, engaging activities that bring out the musicality in everyone - from the youngest member of the family to the oldest. Together you'll learn more about music as you learn more about each other. Children under 9 months accompanying siblings are free! A sibling discount is available for this program. The discount will be applied at the time of registration. (sl)

name: Rhythm Express: Music and Babies

age_range.raw_age_text: Age less than 1y 6m

description: Your musical playgroup awaits! Recent studies have shown that music affects the physical, emotional and intellectual development of babies and children and strengthens cognitive and sensory development. Join other like-minded parents of babies and new walkers as we experience the positive effects of music. Register child only; parents attend for free. A sibling discount is available for this program. The discount will be applied at the time of registration. (sl)

name: RoboThink: Battle Robots Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Calling all future champions and robot enthusiasts! Brace yourself for an action-packed camp at RoboThink, where you'll embark on an epic journey of building and battling with a wide variety of awe-inspiring robots. Put on your engineer's hat and bring your robot to life using gears, motors, axles, and our state-of-the-art hardware. Then engage in thrilling battles and challenges that will push your skills to the limit. No experience necessary just come ready to battle, have fun, and let your robot reign supreme! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Battle Transportation Bots Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Explore the world of transportation with RoboThink as we build Trains, Planes & Automobile robots based on our favorite vehicles from the RoboThink curriculum! In this exciting robotics camp, students will use motors, gears, and mainboards and learn important engineering and robotics concepts as they bring their creations to life and take their STEM skills to new heights. Class often culminates in a friendly, exciting battle, so sign up now for a fun, high-energy week together! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Creative Construction Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: It's construction and demolition time, RoboThink style! We’ll be putting on our hard hats and diving into the world of creative construction by building various machines and even a whole city of your dreams. From operating a dump truck to demolishing structures with a mighty wrecking ball, this camp offers an incredible experience for young builders like you! Don't worry if you've never done it before; with RoboThink by your side, you'll be a construction pro in no time! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Engineer Race Cars Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Rev up your engines and hit the racetrack with RoboThink! Get ready for an adrenaline-pumping program where your student will build and race a fleet of extraordinary race cars. But that's not all! You’ll also dive deep into the fascinating world of automotive engineering, learning about transmissions, pistons, and differentials. Put on your racing gloves and join us for an epic ride! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Intro to Coding Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Dive into the world of coding with RoboThink's Introduction to Coding program! Equipped with RoboThink's special software, your student will discover the fundamental concepts of coding in an engaging and enjoyable environment. From loops and conditions to variables, they'll gain a solid foundation in coding principles. Prepare to build exciting programs, no prior coding experience required, but basic computer skills and reading fluency are necessary. (bd)

name: RoboThink: Jr. STEM Robotics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Want to ignite your child's passion for engineering and robotics at an early age? Look no further than RoboThink Jr.! Our newest program offers young children an exciting introduction to the world of RoboThink robotics, keeping everything simple yet engaging to nurture their creativity. From building and battling tops to using a bow to shoot targets or even playing a board game, your child will have a blast while learning valuable skills, such as focus, problem-solving, creativity, communication and sharing ideals- all skills that prepare them for school and encourage positive learning habits. Get ready for a journey filled with fun, laughter, and educational growth! (bd)

name: RoboThink: Rumble Robotics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: Welcome to Rumble Robotics, where the battleground is set, and the excitement is unmatched! In this high-energy program, students of all skill levels immerse themselves in thrilling battles, whether it's spinning tops, wind-up knights, or their very own handcrafted battle robots. The adrenaline-pumping action unfolds over an hour, offering a perfect blend of strategy, creativity, and friendly competition. No prior experience is required. In this hands-on program, kids build a variety of machines from spirographs to kinetic sculptures that produce real art. Along the way, they explore famous artists and movements like Piet Mondrian’s geometry, Seurat’s pointillism, and Banksy’s street art. Students will also gain foundational knowledge in robotics and engineering concepts like gear ratios, DC motors, and mechanical design all while getting hands-on and having fun. Rugby is a game that welcomes all kids. No prior experience is necessary. Safety and enjoyment are the top priorities. USA Rugby qualified coaches will work with participants to teach positions and rules, while developing skills in passing, tackling, rucking, mauling, scrums, and lineouts to allow for full enjoyment in a safe environment. Participants will have the option to participate in competitive games, where they will compete for the Rugby Illinois State Championship. Games take place on Sundays, within 1-hour drive from Naperville. Each participant will be provided shorts, socks, and a Crusaders T-shirt. Cleats and a mouth guard are required. age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Most exercise classes include stretching during warmup and cool down, but what about an entire class dedicated to this important activity? Stretching is vital for seniors and allows for greater movement in joints while improving overall posture in addition to releasing muscle tension and soreness, reducing the risk of injury. It also may help increase circulation, muscle control and improve balance and coordination. This 30-minute class, taught by Cecilia Floyd-Carruthers, covers stretching exercises from head to toe in a seated position as well as standing, using a chair for balance. Please bring water for hydration and wear gym shoes with good support. In order to participate in the Senior Stretch class, you must be mobile and able to support yourself without assistance. (jg)

name: SHIP-August

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: SHIP is the Illinois State Health Insurance Assistance Program. Whether you are new to Medicare or already enrolled, SHIP is a great way to get information and answers about health insurance coverage for seniors. If you are considering a prescription drug plan, please bring your Medicare card, any other insurance cards and a list of your medications, including dosage and frequency to your appointment. If you would like to see if you might be eligible for financial help in paying for Medicare, bring your most recent tax return. Open Enrollment occurs every year between October 15 and December 7. Appointments during this time frame are for those who would like to review their Medicare Part C coverage or Part D prescription plans to insure you have the most comprehensive, cost efficient coverage for the upcoming year. Information on health insurance coverage for seniors includes the following: Medicare A & B (hospital/doctor), Medicare C (Medicare Advantage Plans/HMO, PPO, PFFS), Medicare D (Prescription Drug Plans), Medicare Supplemental Policies (Medigap), Long Term Care Insurance and Medicaid Programs. Counselors are trained and sponsored by the State of Illinois Department on Aging. Appointments are available between 9:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. To register, call 630-848-5000 or go online to napervilleparks.org to book an appointment with a SHIP counselor. (jg)

name: Tai Chi: Adult & Senior-Practice and Instructional

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Looking for better balance, gentle movement, stress relief and moving meditation? Tai Chi might be just what you are looking for and it will complement your other exercise routines. The many benefits of Tai Chi including maintaining mobility, agility, health and vitality can be found in these simple movements. See why Tai Chi has been practiced for centuries to benefit the mind and body. Practice vs Instructional Classes: Practice classes have minimal instruction allowing the student to just follow along in the various exercises and movements to focus on relaxing and breathing. Every level Practice class has a corresponding level Instructional class. Instructional classes provide detailed explanation of everything contained in the Practice class. Ideally, a student would take both. Adult vs Senior Classes: Adult and Senior Tai Chi classes have the same content and instruction. Senior classes are priced for those 50 and over. Anyone 60 and over can register for an Adult Tai Chi class and receive a 20% senior discount. In Person vs Virtual vs Hybrid: Some classes are in person only; some are virtual only (via Zoom) and some are hybrid. Hybrid classes are simultaneously offered in person and via Zoom. If you cannot attend an in-person class on a specific date, you can participate at home via Zoom. (jg)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: This program is designed to build a solid dance foundation. Dancers learn proper posture and technique while being introduced to dance terminology from both dance styles. The program focuses on the fundamentals of jazz technique, while incorporating tap to help with rhythm, tempo and distribution of weight. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Tap: Adult Beginning

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This tap program presents the rhythms and sounds of tap dance in a fun and upbeat way. As dancers progress, they add on to beginning rhythms and steps while sharpening their memory and improving coordination. Program explores more complex techniques and patterns while challenging the students to open their tap dance movement vocabulary, increasing their confidence and tap dance knowledge. This program is perfect for students new to tap, those looking to return to dance, or wanting to try something new. Please visit our website at www.napervilleparks.org/dance for dress code information. (sl)

name: Tennis: A Taste of Tennis

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: This camp is designed for kids who want a great introduction to tennis. Instruction follows the USTA's 10-and-under pathway which utilizes smaller courts, special balls and smaller racquets. Camp emphasizes the ABCs - agility, balance and coordination. Please wear tennis shoes. In case of rainout, makeup will be on Friday. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Competitive Clinic

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Intermediate Level (NTRP Rating 2.7-3.4) and Advanced level players (NTRP ranking 3.5+) benefit from this clinic that focuses on singles and doubles strategies, shot consistency, specialty shots, difficult shots and serves. Players enrolled at the incorrect level may be removed. In case of rain, one makeup will be held. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Drill & Play

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This class is designed for adults who have progressed beyond the beginner level and are able to rally consistently. Players should be comfortable with the basic strokes and ready to refine their technique while continuing to build confidence and consistency during live play. Instruction will focus on improving stroke mechanics, court positioning, and shot selection. This 90-minute class emphasizes skill development through dynamic drills, point play, and match based situations. Participants will also work on scoring, strategy, and structured match play to support continued growth and on-court decision making. Participants must bring their own racket, water, and gym shoes. One makeup class will be offered in the event of inclement weather. This class is not intended for beginner-level players. (ba)

name: Tennis: Adult Outdoor

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This class is designed for adults who are new to tennis or who have taken one or two beginner classes. Participants will learn the fundamental tennis strokes, including forehands, backhands, volleys, and serves, while developing overall consistency and confidence on the court. Instruction will also cover scoring, rules, and basic match play so players feel comfortable playing points and games. This 90-minute class focuses on development drills and repetition, emphasizing the basics of tennis in a supportive learning environment. Participants must bring their own racquet, water, and gym shoes. One makeup class will be offered in the event of inclement weather. This class is strictly for beginner-level players. (ba)

name: Tennis: Cardio Tennis

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Coaches blast music and fast, tough feeds to get your heart pumping. The NTRP rating of 2.5-3.4 is adhered to as drills are designed for players who already have a foundation of skills and the athleticism to really hustle. Players who are not at an appropriate level are offered alternative program options. Please bring water and a towel. If class is canceled due to weather, one makeup will be held at the end of the session.(ba)

name: Tennis: Junior

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Learn to play or improve your tennis game with the Park District's experienced staff. Students should dress in comfortable clothing, wear tennis shoes and provide their own racquet. Players are grouped by ability. Classes utilize the ABCs - agility, balance and coordination - along with instruction on basic tennis strokes. Orange Ball class will use a 60' tennis court and special orange tennis balls. Green Ball classes will use the Green Ball on a regular court. Yellow Ball classes use a standard tennis ball on a regular court. Beginners have never played tennis or have played a limited amount, but not on a regular basis. Class emphasizes introduction of forehand, backhand, serve, shot placement, positioning, scoring and rules. Advanced Beginners have knowledge of scoring and rules and may have had some lessons, but lack on-court experience. They can keep a ball in play with others of similar ability. Class emphasizes improvement of basic strokes and works on positioning, shot placement, footwork and serve consistency. Intermediates are those who can place shots with moderate success and sustain a rally at a slow pace. They are not yet comfortable with all strokes and lack consistency in serving. In case of rain, up to two makeups will be held at the completion of the session. (ba)

name: Tennis: Little Aces

Children learn basic tennis skills utilizing the USTA's 10-and-under tennis pathway on smaller courts using special racquets and red tennis balls. Children must wear tennis shoes; racquets are provided. In case of rain, one make up will be held at the end of the session.. (ba)

name: Tennis: Parent/Child Learn and Play

Children learn basic tennis skills utilizing the USTA's 10-and-under tennis pathway on smaller courts using special racquets and low-bounce red tennis balls. The second part of the lesson is dedicated to play; first with the child playing with the parent and later playing against other children with the parents as coaches. Children use our special mini racquets; regulation racquets are provided for parents. Fee is per couple; one parent per child registered. In case of rain, up to two makeups will be held at the completion of the session. No class July 1-7. (ba)

Lessons with one of our USPTA/USPTR Certified Pros are $79 per hour. Purchase a five-lesson package and save 10%. Purchase a ten-lesson package and save 15%. name: Friday Night Pickleball Boot Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: This Boot Camp features themes offering drills and specialized match play with pros. Players will be divided by level and placed four to a court with 60 minutes of drilling and 60 minutes of supervised match play. Themes include attacking the return of serve, hitting better third shot drops, varying the pace of the ball and getting to the net faster. Players need to know how to keep score as there will be supervised match play. Boot camps are appropriate Advanced Beginner/Intermediate level players.

name: Friday Night Pickleball Social Club

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Join us for exciting and engaging evenings at the Friday Night Pickleball Club! Whether you're a seasoned player or just starting out, this program offers something for everyone. Half of the gym will be dedicated to open play pickleball, where you can enjoy friendly matches, meet new people, and have fun. Courts will be available for casual games, allowing you to play at your own pace and skill level. The other half of the gym will feature a pickleball pro who is available to answer your questions, help you work on techniques, and go over rules. This is a fantastic opportunity to improve your game, learn new strategies, and get personalized tips from an expert. Light refreshments will be provided throughout the evening, ensuring you stay energized and hydrated while you play and learn. Sign up for the season and enjoy the flexibility of attending at your leisure each Friday. Whether you come every week or just occasionally, the Friday Night Pickleball Club is designed to fit your schedule and provide a welcoming environment for all participants. No Class 7/3.

age_range.raw_age_text: 55 yrs +

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 100 yrs

The Northbrook Speed Skating Club sent athletes to every Winter Olympics for 70 years and in that time span won more Olympic medals than any other Club in US Speedskating. Skaters may be in figure skates, hockey skates or speedskates. Helmet and gloves are required

name: Pickleball Co-Ed League - 60+ Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 60 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court.

name: Taekwondo - Advanced: Red - Black Belts

age_range.raw_age_text: 7 yrs +

description: Taekwondo, one of the newest Olympic sports, is a 2,000-year-old martial art, offering a variety of benefits for people of all ages and physical abilities. Students have the opportunity to improve concentration, self-esteem, achieve lifelong physical fitness, and learn self-defense skills. Classes are taught under the direction of Grand Master Ki Hong Kim (9th Dan Kukkiwon World Taekwondo Headquarters). All students should talk to their instructor on the first day to get sized for a uniform which costs $50 cash or check. Uniforms are required to complete the class and to test for belt rank. Belt testing is offered through KH Kim Taekwondo, at an additional fee. Tests happen at the instructor's discretion when the student has learned the appropriate skills. All green belt students (Ages 7 yrs and up) are required to have complete sparring gear, which is purchased from the Instructor. Students will develop heightened focus, mental discipline, and strategic thinking, while enhancing their cardiovascular conditioning, flexibility, body control, and the beginning of mastery-level material to prepare students not only to earn their black belt, but to embody the role of a martial artist at the highest level. No class 5/25.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: We are celebrating with bubbles, giggles, and hands-on science! Get ready to sip, mix, and experiment your way through a fun soda taste-testing experience; design your own wacky soda brand and mascot in the Fizz Lab; experiment with carbonation at the Candy Creation Soda Station; learn the history of this nostalgic beverage during a pop-up lesson; and leave with a fizzing souvenir surprise.

name: Thrills and Chills of Ice Cream

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Making and eating ice cream is a fun way to introduce kids to early physics and chemistry concepts. Participants will make homemade ice cream without a freezer, explore the science behind classic amusement park treats, and learn how this iconic dessert has evolved over time. The class wraps up with a wildly fun ice cream eating contest—brain freeze included! Expect hands-on learning, plenty of tastings, a themed souvenir, and a delightfully sticky experience.

name: Youth Company-- Head Over Heels (High School Edition)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Come join Northbrook Youth Company Teens to tell a hilarious story with a lot of heart this summer! "Head Over Heels (High School Edition) follows the adventures of a royal family on an wild quest to save their kingdom from vanishing. From family feuds, to secret crushes, to mistaken identities, this musical has something for everyone! Directed by Katie Denten, Rhys Steele, and David Zizic. Auditions will be on July 6 from 3:30 to 5:30pm, with callbacks (as needed) on July 7 from 3:30 to 5:30pm. Beginning on July 8, rehearsals will be Tuesdays-Thursdays from 3:15-6pm. Beginning on July 27, rehearsals will be 3:15-6:30pm. There will also an additional on July 26 from 12:00-5:00pm. Technical rehearsals will be August 10-13 from 3:00-7:00pm, with performances on August 14 and 15 at 7pm, and August 16 at 2pm.

name: Youth Cycling Program

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: The Northbrook Park District offers young athletes interested in competitive cycling an opportunity to focus on training and skills. This is not a learn-to-ride program. Young athletes will focus on training and skills on Wednesday and compete in races on Fridays. Wednesday's trainings cover fitness, bike handling skills, and safety related to racing. Races are both team and individual competitions, with riders assigned to teams every week. The coaching staff will determine race assignments, types, distances, and handicaps. Participation on both Wednesday and Friday is highly encouraged. Coaches will evaluate riders based on riding skill and lap times to assign appropriate group levels. Evaluation continues throughout the season. No class 7/3, 7/24

name: Let's Play Rugby! Arlington Stallions (10-15yrs)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 15 yrs

location: Sunset Meadows Turf and Patriots Park
description: Rugby combines the best attributes of American football, basketball and soccer. This program is designed to teach young boys and girls the basics of the game of rugby and is designed to introduce them to the skills, training, philosophy and strategy necessary to safely participate in this sport, Learn the positions, passing techniques and the rules of the game. The teams will compete in the rugby Illinois/ USA rugby state championship program that ends with a state championship, last weekend of May. Training sessions will typically be held on Monday and Wednesday evenings and are conducted by USA Rugby Certified and Illinois Rugby Registered coaches from the Arlington Stallions Rugby Club. For program information, please contact arlingtonstallionsrugby@gmail.com. (CE)

name: Aces Spring House Soccer - 1st Grade Girls

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 8 yrs

description: HOUSE SOCCER LEAGUE (K-8th Grade) Our house league is designed to introduce and help grow your child’s love for the game of soccer. After registering, your child will be placed on a team based on their age/grade, reciprocal friend request, school, or local community center. Practice locations, days, and times will be determined by your volunteer parent coaches. Each team will have one weekly1-hour practice and one to two games each weekend. Team assignments, practices schedule, and all the other information you’ll need for the season will be sent via email no later than April 3rd. Practices start the week of April 13th and first games are the weekend of April 18th. Dates subject to change. REGISTRATION CLOSES ON MARCH 10th All registrations after this date will be put on our WAITLIST. Our goal is to find as many waitlisted participants roster spots as possible. However, this will only occur after initial teams have been formed. Therefore, friend requests and grouping with classmates may be more difficult to honor. You will be notified via email no later than April 10th that you’ve been placed on a team. You will not be charged for the program while on the waitlist. QUESTIONS? Contact Athletic Supervisor, Laura Husko, at Lhusko@ahpd.org

description: Boat Launching Boaters are allowed to launch their own craft at Lake Arlington. Currently there are no restrictions on size. However, there are no ramps. name: Muskies Swim Team - Boys 11-12's

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. name: Morning Junior Swim School 6/8-6/11 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 8.

name: Morning Swim School 6/8-6/11 - Camelot

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 8

name: Camelot Day Camp Swim Lesson add on - Week 1

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Day Camp and Aquatic Staff work together to transition campers to their lesson. Sign up for one week - or sign up for all of the weeks. We follow our Swim School curriculum. Swim School can be a great compliment to our Interpark Swim Team. If your child is on swim team - we can make sure their swim lesson is adjusted to be taught at a swim team level. Swimming lessons are on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday of this week. There are never swim lessons on Wednesdays due to Day Camp field trips. No swim lessons on Fridays. 5-12yrs – Swim School Swim School is 40 minutes. A 40-minute swim lesson will also help increase and promote positive conditioning of your child’s endurance for other sports and activities outside of the pool. Swim School is a group environment to motivate your child. Our first level begins with correct face and body position, floats, and opening eyes underwater without goggles. Your child will then progress through levels where all the swim strokes are introduced and eventually work towards treading in deep water (an essential life skill), dives, and flip turns (if desired). The instructor typically plays a game using swim school skills or we have fun jumping off the diving boards for the last 5 minutes. Swim School is the perfect time for your child to push past any fears they may have going of the diving board for the first time. We have an instructor in the water to boost confidence. This is an amenity not possible during open swim. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class. We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 1.

name: Morning Swim School 6/8-6/11 - Camelot

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 8

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. name: Evening Swim School 6/8-6/11 - Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 8
