name: Saturday Junior Swim School 6/13 - 8/1 - Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. • Parents or caregivers - please stand or sit at the shallow end of Family Activity Pool. Please do not sit on the benches directly across from your child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class - we turn on the kiddie slide and sprays for fun time. The swim lesson instructor may not be the same each week of this session. We do allow our staff to obtain substitutes if they cannot work. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider signing up for Water Babies instead of Junior Swim School. Please sit on the bleachers on the east end of the pool deck. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s school year! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class. We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session.

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. • Parents or caregivers - please stand or sit at the shallow end of Family Activity Pool. Please do not sit on the benches directly across from your child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class - we turn on the kiddie slide and sprays for fun time. The swim lesson instructor may not be the same each week of this session. We do allow our staff to obtain substitutes if they cannot work. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider signing up for Water Babies instead of Junior Swim School. Please sit on the bleachers on the east end of the pool deck. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s school year! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class. We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Learn the basics of ballet, enjoy outdoor play and create fun crafts in this festive summer camp! All children must also be fully toilet-trained. We suggest a leotard and pink ballet shoes with hair in a ponytail or bun. Dancers may also wear optional tights, skirt, shorts, tutu or ballet dress. Ballet shoes are only for dance time: please be sure to send enclosed gym shoes for outside play and any appropriate layers for cooler days. (KS)

name: Morning Swim School 6/15-6/18 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 15

name: Morning Junior Swim School 6/15-6/18 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 15.

Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. name: Evening Swim School 6/15-6/18 - Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 15

description: Program Details Ages: 3–5 years Class Length: 30 minutes Format: Child-only class (parents/caregivers do not enter the water) Program Overview Junior Swim School is designed for preschool-aged swimmers who are ready to participate in swim lessons independently. For many children, this is their first experience entering the pool without a parent, so instruction focuses on building comfort, confidence, and water familiarity. Skills Taught Instruction progresses at each child’s pace and may include: Getting face and hair wet Front and back floats Kicking and scooping Jumping in from the pool edge Retrieving underwater objects The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Families wishing to be in the water with their child should consider our Water Babies program. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Goggles Policy: Goggles are not recommended for Junior Swim School. Opening eyes underwater is an important skill at this level. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 15

For many children, this is their first experience entering the pool without a parent, so instruction focuses on building comfort, confidence, and water familiarity. Skills Taught Instruction progresses at each child’s pace and may include: Getting face and hair wet Front and back floats Kicking and scooping Jumping in from the pool edge Retrieving underwater objects The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Families wishing to be in the water with their child should consider our Water Babies program. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Goggles Policy: Goggles are not recommended for Junior Swim School. Opening eyes underwater is an important skill at this level. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 15

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: This class focuses on building the muscles and specific technique necessary to begin training for pointe. Students must also be enrolled and attend an additional ballet class. Bone development is taken into consideration when placing students en pointe so dancers must be at least 13 years old before going en pointe. Students should expect to participate in 1-4 sessions of Pointe Prep before being considered for Pointe. It is important to note that every dancer is different and that proper bone development and muscle strength will be a main factor in the placement decision over age or participation. Under no circumstance should students purchase pointe shoes until instructed to do so. Pointe Prep II dancers must be evaluated to enroll. Contact ABraheny@ahpd.org to request an evaluation. Dancers should wear pink ballet shoes, leotard, skirt or dance shorts, and convertible or footless tights (optional). (KS)

name: Morning Junior Swim School 6/22-6/25 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 22.

When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 22

name: The Train Lady's Gardens Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: THE TRAIN LADY’S GARDENS LUNCH IN CHESSIE’S TRAIN CAR Barrington, Illinois Tuesday, June 23, 2026 9:15 AM - 3:00 PM Discover one of the most beautiful venues in the country, featuring 10 acres of landscaped gardens, a 4-acre lake, and an internationally recognized Garden Railway and Model Railroad Museum. Wandering Tree Estate is home to two large and elaborate model railroad layouts. The outdoor layouts include large G-scale trains that traverse bridges, glide over waterfalls, and pass by model vignettes, each telling its own unique story. Inside, the Harvey Silets Memorial Chicago Model Railroad Museum showcases O-scale trains running through a replica of the City of Chicago. After the gardens, enjoy lunch in a train car at Chessie’s Restaurant. Lunch includes a house salad, freshly baked bread and butter, and an ice cream sundae for dessert. Entrée options are: Roasted Pork Loin: slow roasted with a mushroom wine sauce, potato, and fresh vegetable Beef Stroganoff: beef tenderloin strips in a white wine and mushroom sour cream sauce over noodles Chicken Piccata: sautéed breast of chicken, with lemon garlic wine sauce and capers, served over linguine Coffee, tea, and soda are included, and a cash bar will be available.

name: Morning Junior Swim School 6/29-7/2 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 29.

name: Morning Swim School 6/29-7/2 - Camelot

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: June 29

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Day Camp and Aquatic Staff work together to transition campers to their lesson. Sign up for one week - or sign up for all of the weeks. We follow our Swim School curriculum. Swim School can be a great compliment to our Interpark Swim Team. If your child is on swim team - we can make sure their swim lesson is adjusted to be taught at a swim team level. Swimming lessons are on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday of this week. There are never swim lessons on Wednesdays due to Day Camp field trips. No swim lessons on Fridays. 5-12yrs – Swim School Swim School is 40 minutes. A 40-minute swim lesson will also help increase and promote positive conditioning of your child’s endurance for other sports and activities outside of the pool. Swim School is a group environment to motivate your child. Our first level begins with correct face and body position, floats, and opening eyes underwater without goggles. Your child will then progress through levels where all the swim strokes are introduced and eventually work towards treading in deep water (an essential life skill), dives, and flip turns (if desired). The instructor typically plays a game using swim school skills or we have fun jumping off the diving boards for the last 5 minutes. Swim School is the perfect time for your child to push past any fears they may have going of the diving board for the first time. We have an instructor in the water to boost confidence. This is an amenity not possible during open swim. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class. We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 22.

Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. For many children, this is their first experience entering the pool without a parent, so instruction focuses on building comfort, confidence, and water familiarity. Skills Taught Instruction progresses at each child’s pace and may include: Getting face and hair wet Front and back floats Kicking and scooping Jumping in from the pool edge Retrieving underwater objects The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Families wishing to be in the water with their child should consider our Water Babies program. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Goggles Policy: Goggles are not recommended for Junior Swim School. Opening eyes underwater is an important skill at this level. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. name: Pioneer Day Camp Swim Lesson add on - Week 5

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12 yrs

description: Day Camp and Aquatic Staff work together to transition campers to their lesson. Sign up for one week - or sign up for all of the weeks. We follow our Swim School curriculum. Swim School can be a great compliment to our Interpark Swim Team. If your child is on swim team - we can make sure their swim lesson is adjusted to be taught at a swim team level. Swimming lessons are on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday of this week. There are never swim lessons on Wednesdays due to Day Camp field trips. No swim lessons on Fridays. 5-12yrs – Swim School Swim School is 40 minutes. A 40-minute swim lesson will also help increase and promote positive conditioning of your child’s endurance for other sports and activities outside of the pool. Swim School is a group environment to motivate your child. Our first level begins with correct face and body position, floats, and opening eyes underwater without goggles. Your child will then progress through levels where all the swim strokes are introduced and eventually work towards treading in deep water (an essential life skill), dives, and flip turns (if desired). The instructor typically plays a game using swim school skills or we have fun jumping off the diving boards for the last 5 minutes. Swim School is the perfect time for your child to push past any fears they may have going of the diving board for the first time. We have an instructor in the water to boost confidence. This is an amenity not possible during open swim. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class. We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is June 29.

This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/13-7/16 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is July 13.

description: Day Camp and Aquatic Staff work together to transition campers to their lesson. Sign up for one week - or sign up for all of the weeks. We follow our Swim School curriculum. Swim School can be a great compliment to our Interpark Swim Team. If your child is on swim team - we can make sure their swim lesson is adjusted to be taught at a swim team level. Swimming lessons are on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday of this week. There are never swim lessons on Wednesdays due to Day Camp field trips. No swim lessons on Fridays. 5-12yrs – Swim School Swim School is 40 minutes. A 40-minute swim lesson will also help increase and promote positive conditioning of your child’s endurance for other sports and activities outside of the pool. Swim School is a group environment to motivate your child. Our first level begins with correct face and body position, floats, and opening eyes underwater without goggles. Your child will then progress through levels where all the swim strokes are introduced and eventually work towards treading in deep water (an essential life skill), dives, and flip turns (if desired). The instructor typically plays a game using swim school skills or we have fun jumping off the diving boards for the last 5 minutes. Swim School is the perfect time for your child to push past any fears they may have going of the diving board for the first time. We have an instructor in the water to boost confidence. This is an amenity not possible during open swim. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 20

name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/20-7/23 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is July 20.
