Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. name: Evening Swim School 7/20-7/23 - Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 20

For many children, this is their first experience entering the pool without a parent, so instruction focuses on building comfort, confidence, and water familiarity. Skills Taught Instruction progresses at each child’s pace and may include: Getting face and hair wet Front and back floats Kicking and scooping Jumping in from the pool edge Retrieving underwater objects The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Goggles Policy: Goggles are not recommended for Junior Swim School. Opening eyes underwater is an important skill at this level. name: Pee Wee Pickleball

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Join us for a fun, active class where children can learn the basics of pickleball. This class is perfect for younger players who have never played pickleball before or are just starting out. We’ll focus on how to hit the ball with a paddle, take turns and move around the court. With easy games and playful activities, kids will practice skills like swinging, bouncing and hitting the ball over a low net. We’ll also learn to play together as a team and take turns in a fun, friendly way. This class will be full of games, colorful balls and lots of smiles. Age appropriate equipment will be provided. Please bring a labeled water bottle. (MH)

name: Junior Pickleball

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: This class will introduce youngsters to the basics of pickleball such as grip, scoring, forehand and backhand shots, ball return, dinks and other shots needed to play this easy to learn sport. Fun and challenging drills and games will help kids develop the space management, movement skills, and mental abilities needed for a successful pickleball game. All equipment will be provided. Please bring a labeled water bottle. (MH)

name: Youth Pickleball

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Ready to try the fastest growing sport in America? Pickleball is a fun sport that combines many elements of tennis, badminton and ping pong. Pickleball can be enjoyed by all ages and skill levels and is a fantastic hobby for young players for the same reason it is great for adults. The nature of the game is a strong equalizer from a skill-based perspective. We will cover pickleball basics such as grip, ground strokes, dink shot, serving, lob shot and court positioning. Players will also learn scoring and pickleball rules as well as have plenty of time for game play. Please bring a water bottle. Equipment will be provided. (MH)

name: Teen Pickleball

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 17y 11m

description: Come be a part of the pickleball craze! Teens will work on foundational skills such as the ready position, how to hold a paddle and techniques for serves, returns, dinks and volleys. They will also learn footwork, scoring, rules and tactics and will be challenged through teamwork, endurance, speed and coordination. Each class will involve drills and game play. This program aims to ignite a passion for the sport of pickleball while establishing a strong mechanical foundation for each player. Bring a labeled water bottle. Equipment will be provided. No class June 30 & July 2. (MH)

name: The Thrills and Chills of Ice Cream - Life Coaching for Kids

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Making and eating ice cream is a fun way to introduce early physics and chemistry teachings to children. Kids can become an expert on this beloved treat and billion-dollar business as we make a batch of homemade ice cream without using a freezer! Also, explore the science of amusement park treats and the first ice cream novelty treat invented on a stick. Then sit down for the most outrageous ice cream eating contest in town. Did anyone say BRAIN FREEZE? Who will be crowned King or Queen? This is a child’s dream class and all about putting the fun back into learning and building self-esteem. This class explores both Chemical and Industrial Engineering concepts, along with how this treat evolved. Don’t wear your Sunday best to this event, we will get sticky! Lots of tastings, contests, and a themed souvenir included. Instructor: Lisa Lombardi Coaching Inc, www.lisalombardi.com. This is a drop off class. (CH)

With hands-on guidance, kids will also get help riding down small ramps as they build comfort and confidence. Skaters must bring a drink and wear a helmet. Knee, elbow, and wrist guards encouraged. name: Morning Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 27

name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Heritage

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: • 3-5 yrs • 30 minutes • Parents or caregivers are not allowed in the water with child. For most - it's the first time a child enters a pool without a parent so we begin by making your child feel comfortable. This may look like simply focusing on getting the face and hair wet at first, which can be scary for some. Then progressing through supported floats, bobs, kick board use, jumping in the water from side of pool, and eventually swimming 3 yards with no assistance under water. Last five minutes of class is fun time and games. POPULAR QUESTIONS: Can I sit on the pool deck and watch my child’s swim lesson? Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. These classes are intended to separate the child and parent so the teaching environment has less interruptions and improved focus to achieve better learning for all participants. If you are looking to be within arm’s reach or close enough to talk with your child during each swim lesson, please consider purchasing a Water Babies Punch Card. Parents can be in the water with their child in a Water Babies class, unlike Junior Swim School. Less interruptions and distractions from parents will allow teachers to have a more productive 30-minute lesson for everyone in their group. Help us help your child. Less interruptions. Improved focus. Better learning. My child would like specifically either a boy or girl instructor or I want a specific instructor. We recommend considering “Pop-up” Private Swim Lessons which give you the option to hand select your child’s teacher. It is not possible to select a specific instructor for group lessons. Who is teaching my child? Almost all of our instructors are currently high school or college students. Their energy is through the roof and they love their jobs and working with kids. Many are high school and college swimmers and quite a few are interested in a career specializing in early childhood and/or teaching. We aim for our swimming lesson program to be a highlight of your child’s summer! That is only possible because of our young staff. For many, this is their first job and they are eager to succeed. Can my child wear goggles? In Junior Swim School we recommend no goggles. Becoming dependent on goggles will not help your child adapt and feel comfortable in water as they grow older. Opening eyes underwater is a skill in Junior Swim School. Goggles are also not allowed on our diving boards or slides. We want your child’s first experience going off the diving board to be positive and feel familiar underwater. Often times the child who panics after going of the diving board for the first time has never felt the sensation of being underwater with no goggles. Swimming Lesson Code of Conduct – please read to make sure our program is the right fit for your family. To participate in group swimming lessons your child needs to be able to stay with their group and follow directions from all aquatic staff (instructors and lifeguards). When our swim lesson instructors are working on a skill with a child – the instructor can be up to 15 yards away from the other children in the group. Our beginner swimmers who cannot swim without assistance need to have the muscle tone and strength to do the following when it is not their turn with their instructor: 1. Sit on the ledge of the pool 2. Stand on the in-water riser if they are being used 3. Stay put, above water, in their spot in our “zero-depth”, in-water bench area, or stairs that lead into the pool. When a child moves from their spot and either jumps or slips underwater, we have lifeguards on duty; however, lifeguards are scanning a zone of protection, and have 30 seconds to respond to a swimmer who is underwater or in distress. When a child walks or swims away from the group, this puts every child in the group in danger. When an instructor has to take extra time to retrieve the child who has swam away, it also takes class instruction time away from everyone. If your child does not have the strength or muscle tone to stay above water when it is not their turn, is requiring excessive one-on-one attention from the instructor, or is disruptive to the other children, we will offer you a prorated refund and remove your child from the class . We will discuss other options for swim lessons to keep your child swimming safely. We do take water safety very serious and we appreciate that these policies we have in place for in-water instruction are very well received by the majority of parents. If you are unsure about your child’s ability to stay above water when it is not their turn, we do offer one-on-one private swim lesson instruction and/or coaching – with no other children in your child’s session. The last day to request a refund for this class is July 27.

name: Morning Junior Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Heritage

Junior Swim School is one of Arlington Heights Park District’s many “without parent” classes we offer for 3-5 year olds. Such as our ballet and gymnastics classes for this same age. name: Evening Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Frontier

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Program Details Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught <>Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. Early levels focus on foundational skills, including: Proper face and body position Survival floating Breath control As swimmers progress, instructors introduce and refine all major swim strokes, along with: Lateral breathing Deep-water treading Diving The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Safety & Participation Expectations To participate in group lessons, children must be able to: Stay with their group Follow directions from aquatic staff Remain safely above water while waiting their turn (sitting on the ledge, standing on in-water risers, or staying in designated shallow areas) Children who are unable to meet these expectations, require excessive one-on-one attention, or disrupt group safety may be removed from the class and issued a prorated refund. Private lessons may be recommended as an alternative. Refund Policy Last day to request a refund: July 27

name: Evening Junior Swim School 7/27-7/30 - Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

For many children, this is their first experience entering the pool without a parent, so instruction focuses on building comfort, confidence, and water familiarity. Skills Taught Instruction progresses at each child’s pace and may include: Getting face and hair wet Front and back floats Kicking and scooping Jumping in from the pool edge Retrieving underwater objects The final five minutes of each class are dedicated to supervised games and fun time. Important Notes Parent Observation: Parents and caregivers may observe from the pool deck. This “without parent” format helps reduce distractions and allows instructors to maintain focus for a productive learning environment. Families wishing to be in the water with their child should consider our Water Babies program. Instructor Information: Most instructors are high school or college students who enjoy working with children. Many are swimmers or pursuing careers in education or early childhood development. Instructor requests cannot be accommodated for group lessons. Goggles Policy: Goggles are not recommended for Junior Swim School. Opening eyes underwater is an important skill at this level. name: Adult Ballet

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: Beginning level classes focus on the basics of ballet including proper placement and posture; body positions, plies, tendus, battements, and port de bras. Emphasis will be placed on understanding technique, as well as instilling an appreciation and enjoyment of the movement. Advanced levels are a continual study of fundamentals, extended to emotional expression and precision, as well as developing fluid artistic control. Ballet is the basis of all other dance forms and can strongly enhance any athletic activity. We strongly encourage that ballet be taken in conjunction with any other dance class.

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Bachata is a dance that is based on an easy-to-follow sequence of three on-beat steps, with a tap marking the fourth beat. It is styled with a fluid sway of the hips which is mesmerizing to watch and just wonderful to dance! Bachata’s simplicity makes it a beginner-friendly dance, while the opportunity for musical interpretation it provides makes it truly addictive for dancers of all levels. Class is open to individuals and couples. We recommend that you avoid wearing gym shoes to sessions so you can turn smoothly on the floor.

Advanced levels are a continual study of fundamentals, extended to emotional expression and precision, as well as developing fluid artistic control. Ballet is the basis of all other dance forms and can strongly enhance any athletic activity. We strongly encourage that ballet be taken in conjunction with any other dance class.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 7 yrs

description: Does your child dream of twirling like a ballerina or grooving to the latest beats? Our Dance Sampler Camp is the perfect way to ignite their passion for dance! This exciting program lets them explore a variety of styles – ballet, tap, jazz, and even hip-hop – in a fun and supportive environment. Our experienced instructor will guide them every step of the way, building confidence, fostering friendships, and helping them discover their inner star. It's the perfect opportunity to step into the spotlight and begin their dance journey! Dress in comfortable clothes and tap shoes. No previous dance experience needed. There will be a short performance on the last day of class. Ages 7-10

name: Fahrrad Tour Von Schaumburg Bike Ride

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: New Location: The Reconstruction project for the Robert O. Atcher Municipal Center is currently in progress. Due to the ongoing reconstruction project at the Robert O. Atcher Municipal Center, event check-in, departure and return will take place in the parking lot of the Jerry Handlon Administration Building, 235 E. Beech Dr. (a short walk from the MRC outdoor field). Celebrate Schaumburg’s German heritage with a police-guided, one-hour tour of its bikeways. This bike tour is over five miles. Beginners and riders with training wheels are not advised to participate. Please join us after the race for a hot dog or brat. Parking will be available at Meineke Recreation Center at a first come, first served basis, however it is a small lot so we recommend carpooling if possible. Bicyclists must arrive for check-in before we begin our bike tour. Registration begins at 10:30 a.m. and the bike tour departs promptly at 11 a.m. This event is sponsored by Ascension .

Listen for the summer chorus of insects, watch for hopping frogs and smell the fresh air during the full moon. After our hike, enjoy a small snack by a delightful campfire. This family experience is best suited for children ages 5-12. Only register each participating child. Meet at the Nature Center. Ages: 5-12 with adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 10 yrs +

This class helps improve turnout, increase mobility and flexibility, build strength, enhance coordination and fine-tune proprioception.

name: Hip Hop Adult

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, hip-hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

name: Lucky Ducky Race

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: It's time to gather your friends and family for the most adorable race of the year! Watch as rubber ducks take the pool, racing for the title of "Champion Duck!" The top 3 fastest ducks take home a fabulous prize! Bring your family, friends, and a competitive spirit for a race like no other. The duck race will take place during the first 40 minutes of the event. Afterward, enjoy duck themed activities in the pool and music from a live DJ. Registration includes 1 duck and a goodie bag. Additional ducks can be purchased for $4 each, or three for $10. Day of purchases can be made for $8 per duck, or three for $15. Please note: event registration is required to participate in the race. Children 8 years and younger must be accompanied and supervised by a guardian 16 years of age or older at all times. A swimsuit and clean attire are required to enter the pools. Please bring your own towel. Pre-registration is required.

name: Lyrical Beginning 1/2

age_range.raw_age_text: 8 yrs +

description: Lyrical is a merging of both ballet and jazz styles of dance, combining jazz skills with the ease and gracefulness of ballet. This style of dance focuses on an emotional connection to the lyrics of a song and expressing that through movement. This challenges the student to connect on a deeper level to the dance and to become a part of the music.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6y 10m but less than 13 yrs

Learn fundamentals of computer networking through this unique Minecraft experience that also allows you and your friends to work in multiplayer mode as you mine, craft and build together to survive.

name: Mini Ballet

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: Beginning level classes focus on the basics of ballet including proper placement and posture; body positions, plies, tendus, battements, and port de bras. Emphasis will be placed on understanding technique, as well as instilling an appreciation and enjoyment of the movement. Advanced levels are a continual study of fundamentals, extended to emotional expression and precision, as well as developing fluid artistic control. Ballet is the basis of all other dance forms and can strongly enhance any athletic activity. We strongly encourage that ballet be taken in conjunction with any other dance class.

name: Mini Hip Hop

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, Hip-Hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

name: Mini Jazz

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

All jazz classes will have a strong foundation in ballet with an emphasis on correct body alignment and technique. Jazz classes focus on isolations, turns, jumps, leaps, increased flexibility, strength and an overall development of style.

This summer theatre camp is a two week long full-day program that incorporates acting, singing, dancing, sets, props, and costumes, just like a traditional musical! The two week-camp will be followed by two full-scale performances on our main stage! Synopsis: Once upon a time, in a far away swamp, there lived an ogre named Shrek. One day, Shrek finds his swamp invaded by banished fairytale misfits who have been cast off by Lord Farquaad, a tiny terror with big ambitions. When Shrek sets off with a wisecracking donkey to confront Farquaad, he's handed a task — if he rescues feisty princess Fiona, his swamp will be righted. Shrek tries to win Fiona’s love and vanquish Lord Farquaad, but a fairytale wouldn't be complete without a few twists and turns along the way. Performances will take place Friday, July 31st at 7:00pm and Saturday, August 1st at 2:00pm. Just like a traditional show, all campers are expected to be at both performances. Tickets will be available for $7.00 per ticket! Remember to pack a water bottle, lunch and a snack, sunscreen, a pencil and an eraser for your camper. Close-toed shoes are required!

name: From River to Roastery - A Day Exploring Chicago

age_range.raw_age_text: 21 yrs +

description: This day trip offers an engaging exploration of some of Chicago’s most unique urban attractions. Participants will begin at Chicago’s Wild Mile, the world’s first floating eco-park, where they can experience innovative river restoration efforts, enjoy scenic views, and learn about local ecology and sustainability initiatives on a guided tour. The trip continues to Washington Hall, a vibrant culinary destination featuring a variety of local vendors and diverse cuisines, for lunch on your own. The day concludes at the iconic Starbucks Reserve Roastery, where participants can experience small-batch coffee roasting, specialty beverages, and the immersive design of one of Starbucks’ flagship locations. This program blends environmental education, cultural exploration, and culinary discovery for a memorable Chicago experience. Trip includes transportation and guided tour of the Wild Mile. Purchases at Washington Hall and Starbucks Reserve Roastery are on your own. Registration deadline is September 1. (AS)

name: Garden Plots

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: REGISTRATION FOR NEW GARDENERS STARTS MARCH 19 at 8 am! Grow your own produce in an approximately 20' X 20' Elmhurst Garden Plot at Marjorie Davis Park. The Park District will rototill and stake each area, you plant, cultivate and reap the harvest. Six water taps are available and are open 9 am - 9 pm, seven days a week. Weather permitting, growing season runs from May - November 1. A maximum of one garden plot per family is allowed. RETURNING PARTICIPANTS: We will continue to give returning customers (those who had plots in 2025) the option of keeping the same plot or entering the lottery for a new plot. Returning participants must register between February 21-March 13 to secure a plot for 2026. NEW PARTICIPANTS: Those who did not have a plot in 2025 WILL BE ABLE TO REGISTER BETWEEN MARCH 19 (Beginning at 8 am) AND APRIL 5 for any available plots. Available plots will be sold on a first come first served basis. A lottery will be held for plot selection. New gardeners that get a plot will receive more information on how the lottery to choose your plot works after April 5. The lottery for plot selection will be held on Wednesday, April 15 at 6:30 pm at the Kies Recreation Center. (AS)

Gymnasts will begin working on connecting skills as well as flip flops, back walkovers and limbers. Classes are one hour twenty-five minutes in length. Prerequisite: Approval from Girls Intermediate. On vault, students will learn how to run and jump on the springboard, working on a good stick landing. On bars the focus is basic hanging and support skills. On balance beam, posture, balance and a variety of basic skills will be introduced. On floor the focus will be rolls, cartwheels, handstands and jumps. (KG)

Participants can expect to refine the three-step approach on the board with jump, learn the three-step approach with a dive and be introduced to front skills (tuck/pike dive, somersault) and back skills (back jump/dive). Advanced participants will learn a four-step approach. (JME) In order to receive the 10% discount, pool pass purchase transaction must be complete before registration for this class.

name: Intro to Cheer & Poms

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Get ready to jump, shout, and shake those poms! This high-energy class is perfect for young athletes who want to explore the exciting world of cheerleading and poms. In this fun and encouraging environment, kids will learn basic cheer motions, jumps, and chants, pom dance routines set to upbeat, kid-friendly music, and more. This class will spend the first 4 weeks on Poms skills in the dance studio and the second 4 weeks in the Gymnastics Center working on cheer. (KG)

name: Intro to Gymnastics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 4 yrs

description: Intro to Gymnastics is designed for 3 year old gymnasts that might not be ready for class without their parents/guardians. This class will work on easing the gymnasts into a class without their parent/guardian in attendance. Parents/guardians will be required to attend the first 2 classes with their gymnast. The second 2 classes, the parents/guardians will remain in the class, but sitting on the side. For the remainder of the session, the gymnasts will be working with the instructors on their own. Parents/guardians will be able to remain on the side of the class for as long as the gymnast needs them. One parent/guardian will be allowed for each registered gymnast. Siblings will only be allowed in this class if they are able to remain in a baby carrier for the duration of class. (KG)

name: Intro to Turf & Surf Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Introduction to Turf & Surf is the perfect chance to try out this camp at a slower pace. We'll explore local parks and outside activities while learning about bike safety and rules of the road. This camp will offer campers the freedom of jumping on their bikes with friends and counselors and heading out to local destinations 3-5 miles in distance one way, at a casual pace. This program combines hands-on experience to prepare you for future weeks of Turf & Surf camp! Each morning you'll hit the turf with your bike and visit local destinations for a fun, outdoor field trip adventure! After lunch we'll bike over to the pool for swimming. (TGR) PLEASE NOTE: Participants may bike in adverse weather conditions from time to time. All campers are required to have a working, geared bike, bike lock, helmet, water bottle and backpack. Participants will not be permitted to ride without a helmet and should bring a sack lunch and snack each day. A $100 deposit per child per week will be charged at time of registration. The remaining balance will be placed on a payment plan. WITHDRAWAL/REFUND POLICY: In the event you need to cancel a camp, please do so immediately. Withdrawals can be done online through your online account or by submitting a Camp Withdrawal Form (https://www.epd.org/programs/camps) to the registration office at registration@epd.org, or by calling (630) 993-8900. age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 2y 6m but less than 4 yrs

description: With a focus on developing creativity, coordination, balance and self-expression, Itty Bitty Ballet provides a fun environment for your young dancer. Basic ballet steps skills will be explored through imaginative exercises. Participants attend class without parent. Pull-ups are permitted and parent/caregiver must remain in the lobby and be available to change their child. (KG)

name: Junior Lifeguard Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 16 yrs

description: The Junior Lifeguard Camp is for individuals between the ages of 10-15 who are interested in a future of lifeguarding. In this camp they will learn basic aquatic lifesaving skills and first aid for minors. The program will include guidance, challenges, and activities for those interested in furthering their experience in lifeguarding. Participants do not have to have any previous experience in lifesaving skills or first aid, but should be comfortable in the water and have basic swimming skills. (JME) WITHDRAWAL/REFUND POLICY: In the event you need to cancel a camp, please do so immediately. name: Junior Parks & Recreation Professionals

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Ever wonder what it’s like to work for a park district? Go behind the scenes and explore the many exciting careers that keep our parks, playgrounds, and programs running. Participants will learn conduct a playground safety inspection, help plan a special event or class, assist with horticulture projects, and practice interviewing for different park district jobs. Hands-on and interactive, this program is perfect for kids who love to lead, create and explore. (JM)

name: Kitten Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Courts Plus is partnering with St. Sophia's Forgotten Felines to bring you a purr-fectly playful yoga experience! Courts Plus Yoga Instructor will guide you through your practice while adorable kittens roam the room. Yogi's are welcome to play, cuddle and enjoy kitten company throughout their practice. Enjoy gentle movement, lots of smiles and giggles and plenty of kitten energy. Fell in love? Kittens will be available for same-day adoption. Participants interested in adopting that day should complete an adoption application in advance at stsff.com and plan to bring a cat carrier (cardboard carriers will also be available for $10).

name: Lasers-Boys Gymnastics

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Great for boys transitioning out of Asteroids. Swinging, climbing, jumping and building confidence is what Lasers is all about! Gymnastics will be introduced on the six men's events as well as development of basic skills and body positions. All gymnasts must be picked up at the gymnastics doors. (KG)

name: Learn to Sign - ASL (American Sign Language)

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Join us in this fun, interactive and lively class where you will learn to communicate with others through sign language! Each session covers new material. Taught live on the Zoom platform by a Language in Action, Inc. instructor. Zoom login information will be emailed to participants before the first class. (AS)

name: Line Dancing

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: No partner? No problem! Learn today’s hottest line dances from Chicago’s saloons and dance clubs—set to both country and non-country hits. This friendly, low-impact class is a blast, and it’s great for your brain, memory, and overall fitness. Get moving, have fun, and enjoy a low-impact workout that keeps you smiling. (AS)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 2y 6m but less than 3y 7m

description: Little Bug Alone is designed for older two and younger three-year-olds who have adjusted to taking classes independently. Children will enjoy both indoor and outdoor activities that focus on arts & crafts, music & movement, stories & songs and motor skill development. Each week brings a new theme to explore. Children enrolled in Little Bug Alone should be working towards bathroom independence. Pull-ups are permitted, parent/guardian must be available to change within fifteen minutes. age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 7 yrs

Improved self-esteem enables children to better confront peer pressure and to pursue success in all aspects of their lives.

This is an adult/child class; an adult must attend and engage with and help to lead their child in this class. (KG)

name: Memoir Writing

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Everyone has a story to tell—this class will help you find the words to tell yours. Each week, participants will write a 500-word personal essay inspired by their own life experiences. The instructor will provide optional weekly prompts to help spark memories and guide your writing. You'll have the chance to share your work in a supportive, close-knit group and receive thoughtful editing and feedback. Whether you're new to memoir writing or continuing your journey, this class offers a welcoming space to reflect, write, and connect. No previous attendance is required—each session stands on its own. (AS)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: MINI FUNSEEKERS campers should be entering Preschool or Kindergarten in Fall 2026. This camp provides an action packed, full day of camp for 4 and 5-year-olds. Campers will spend most of the time outdoors with age appropriate activities and themes. Each week campers will be visited by a special guest for an in-house field trip. Campers will also visit the spray ground twice a week. Our daily schedule does include rest time. Staff to camper ratio is 1:5. (TGR) All campers should bring a sack lunch, water bottle, towel, and sunscreen every day. There is no camp on July 3. Drop off in the morning is between 8:45-9:15 A.M. and pick-up in the afternoon is 2:45-3:15 P.M. A $100 deposit per child per week will be charged at time of registration. The remaining balance will be put on a payment plan. WITHDRAWAL/REFUND POLICY: In the event you need to cancel a camp, please do so immediately. name: Music Together: Summer

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6m but less than 6 yrs

description: Our upcoming Kazoo Collection features the Music Together® classic “Me, You, and We,” along with beloved favorites like “See the Pony Galloping” and the Spanish folksong “Tingalayo.” Families will enjoy bringing music to life as we dramatize the nursery rhyme “Old King Cole” and sing about favorite foods in “Apples and Cherries.” This six-week class is designed for children from birth through age five and is grounded in child development research. Our family-style learning environment supports natural musical growth—young children learn through observation and imitation, while older children build confidence and leadership skills. Parents and caregivers love the ease of bringing siblings together to one joyful class. Each 45-minute session invites children to participate at their own pace through singing, movement, chanting, listening, and hands-on instrument exploration. We welcome the whole family—parents, grandparents, and caregivers—to share in this engaging and enriching musical experience together. Sibling under 6-months and over 6-years are free with a paid sibling. Materials are provided for home use.

name: Nature Night At Eldridge Park

age_range.raw_age_text: All ages

description: Experience the outdoors after dark during this special Parks & Recreation Month event. Enjoy a guided night walk to explore nocturnal sights and sounds, check out a fascinating bug display, create a glowing lantern craft, and gather around the fire for classic s'mores. A cozy, hands-on evening adventure for nature lovers of all ages. (KG/TGI/ST) Pre-registration is required for all participants.

name: Old Fashioned Fun - Root Beer Float Day

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Celebrate the sweet, fizzy fun of National Root Beer Float Day with a classic treat everyone loves! Join us as we scoop creamy vanilla ice cream and pour ice-cold root beer to create the perfect float. Participants will learn a bit about the history of this all-American dessert while enjoying a refreshing drink and good company. This program is a fun, nostalgic way to cool off, spark conversation, and indulge in a timeless favorite. All supplies provided—just bring your sweet tooth! Registration deadline is one week prior. (AS)

name: Outdoor Bootcamp with Coach Alex

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Get ready to sweat, move and feel strong in this high-energy outdoor bootcamp led by certified personal trainer Alex Blunt. This class combines dynamic bodyweight exercises as well as utilizing select equipment to deliver a full-body workout that builds strength, endurance and confidence, leaving you with that post-workout glow. Expect a mix of cardio, strength and functional movements, all set in the fresh air. Come ready to work hard, have fun and leave feeling accomplished. Class will meet in the new turf area located outside the pool windows. In case of inclement weather, class will be held indoors in the Fitness Studio.

description: Relax and de-stress with a Sunset Sound Bath Meditation in the beautiful Wilder Park Formal Gardens (next to the conservatory building). Experience the mental and physical health benefits of live sound meditation as you are guided on a journey in sound and deep listening by Certified Sound Bath and Meditation facilitator Dana Kraszczynski. A Sound Bath, or Sound Meditation, is a deep immersion in sound that is felt in your whole being. Find a comfortable seat or lie down and allow the soothing vibrations of singing bowls, flutes, and chimes to wash over your whole body, creating a gentle yet deeply transformative effect on your body and mind. The intention of this practice is to guide you into a state of deep relaxation. No special skills, abilities, or beliefs are required to receive the benefits. Please bring something comfortable to sit or lay down on such as a yoga mat, camp chair, blankets, and/or pillows.

Full camp session fee is non-refundable once final payment is scheduled to be collected (one week prior to each camp session). The registration receipt may not reflect exact days registered for. Lake Geneva.

name: August Trip - RT 66 100 Year Celebration Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Step back in time and celebrate 100 years of America’s Mother Road on this comfortable, fully guided Route 66 motorcoach bus tour filled with nostalgia, history, and classic roadside charm. We begin at the Joliet Area Historical Museum , where we’ll pick up our tour guide, Ed . Along the way, we’ll visit the Elwood Arsenal Wayside and the Midewin Tallgrass Prairie Visitor Center . Photo stops include the famous Gemini Giant and the colorful Polka Dot Diner . In Gardner , we’ll see the old two-cell jail , Old Streetcar Diner , and stop at The Shop on 66 for local Route 66 history. Lunch is at the classic Old Route 66 Diner , followed by a stop at the restored gas station in Odell . We’ll finish the day in Pontiac with time for walking, shopping, and visits to the Route 66 Suspension Bridge and Old Sheriff’s Building . Tour, lunch, and transportation included. RT 66.

name: August Trip - Ukulele Moonshiners at White Pines

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

Lunch before the show on your own. Show and transportation included. Wilmette.

description: Get ready to laugh the summer away with nuns from the Little Sisters of Hoboken. This beloved revue will have you in stitches as the five sisters stage a variety show fundraiser filled with outrageous musical numbers and zany comedy. Lunch before the show. Lunch, show and transportation included. Oak Brook.

name: July Trip - Wizard of Oz at The Metropolis

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: We're off to see the wizard! Click your heels three times to join the Cowardly Lion, the Scarecrow, the Tin Man, Dorothy... and Toto too, as they follow the yellow brick road in search of their heart's desires. Lunch on your own at a local restaurant before the show. Show and transportation included. Arlington Heights.

name: July Trip- Stronghold Castle

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: On a bluff high above the Rock River sits the Stronghold Castle. Built in 1928 as a summer retreat for owners of the Chicago Daily News Walter and Josephine Strong, this Tudor style home boasts 16 bedrooms, 9 bathrooms, several fireplaces, secret passages, a pool and tennis courts. Learn about the Strong family, the process of building the castle, depression era history and medieval life. Lunch after the tour on your own. Tour and transportation included. Oregon.

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Cheer on our boys in blue as we head to Wrigley North on a Motorcoach to watch the Cubs battle the Brewers in Milwaukee. Enjoy a great view from your shaded seats along the third base line. Grab a brat or some cheese curds and let's fly the W on the way home! Tickets and Motorcoach transportation included. Milwaukee.

name: June Trip - Fireboat Tour on Lake Michigan

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Join expert docents to learn about Chicago’s world famous architecture, as well as the history of the boat as you cruise along the Chicago River and Lake Michigan. This floating museum showcases photographs of the boat in action, firefighting artifacts, and gives a glimpse of what is was like to be a firefighter stationed on the boat. Lunch before the cruise on your own. Tour and transportation included. Chicago.

name: June Trip - Mystery Trip

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Hop on board for an adventure full of surprises! The destination is under wraps adding an extra layer of excitement and anticipation. Sit back, relax, and enjoy the journey as you’re whisked away to a fun, carefully planned outing—you won’t know where you’re headed, but you can count on a memorable experience! Lunch on your own during the trip.

name: June Trip - South Pacific at Paramount

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Set in a tropical paradise with warm sea breezes, breathless sunsets and B-29 Bombers. experience an uplifting musical tale that follows World War II Armed Services personnel, Ensign Nellie Forbush and Lt. Joseph Cable through spy missions, war-time drama and romance. Balancing duties to their country with their island expectations, they each find themselves irresistibly falling i n love on foreign soil. Lunch in the Meyer Ballroom before the show. Lunch, show, and transportation included. Aurora.

name: June Trip - The Last Five Years at Oil Lamp Theater

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: This widely beloved show takes audiences on the romantic rollercoaster of Jamie and Cathy as they fall in… and out of love over the last five years. Told from each individual’s perspective – one chronologically and one backwards. Be swept into the unique storytelling and find an anti-love story full of humor and heart. Show and transportation included. Glenview.

name: June Trip - Yacht Rock at Rosewood Theater

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Relax and enjoy soft rock music characterized by beaches, summer sun, water, boats and fun! No shoes, no shirt, no problem - dancing is mandatory! Songs by the Beach Boys, Toto, the Bee Gees, Jimmy Buffett, ABBA, Earth, Wind and Fire, and more. Before the show, indulge in chef-attended made to order stations including pasta, sirloin and pork loin, vegetable, salad and desserts. Lunch, show, and transportation included. Delavan, Wi.

name: Kindergarten Flex Camp 2026 - 8:30am-3pm - Entering KDG

age_range.raw_age_text: Age At least 5 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Make your summer a journey to remember! Campers will participate in lively group games, arts & crafts, science experiments, minigolf, walking field trips and splashtacular water fun. There's plenty of time to hang out and make new friends on these daily escapades. Schedule your child's day of fun around your family summer schedule by registering for 2, 3, 4, or 5-day camp each week. Register early as camps fill quickly, there will not be a waitlist option available for Flex Camps. Swim weekly at Swanson Pool. Before and After Camp available, must sign up for the same days registered for all day camps. Fee includes walking trip admissions. Camp meets in Pottawatomie Community Center with convenient door drop off/pick up during regular camp hours. • Campers must purchase and wear a camp t-shirt, comfortable clothing and athletic-style shoes. No sandals. • Bring to camp every day: sack lunch, swim suit, water bottle, sun screen & bug spray • On inclement weather days, camps will meet inside. • Camp counselors have experience working with children and are trained in CPR & First Aid. A $25 initial payment per child per week will be charged at time of registration, and non-refundable beginning May 1. Each schedule change beginning May 1 will incur a $7 processing fee. Transfers, change and refund requests must be made in writing to registration@stcparks.org before the final payment is collected. Full camp session fee is non-refundable once final payment is scheduled to be collected (one week prior to each camp session). The registration receipt may not reflect exact days registered for. For the most accurate information, view the family member's schedule on your park district account. Instructions available in the Summer Camp FAQ's. https://www.stcparks.org/summer-camp-faq/

name: Lifeguard Training Course

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Lifeguards play an important role in a swimming facility's risk management program. Successful participants will become certified lifeguards with the Starguard Elite Lifeguard Program. The course curriculum includes water safety, rescue techniques, basic first aid, Professional Rescuer CPR, AED certification and emergency oxygen support training. Course completion does not guarantee employment with the park district or area aquatic facilities. Payment of the course fee is not a guarantee of certification. Prerequisites: 15 years of age or older before course begins, swim 200 continuous yards using front crawl or breaststroke, tread water for 2 minutes using legs only, feet first surface dive to retrieve a 10-lb. brick from a depth of 12 ft.

name: Lunch and Learn - Finding Joy in Your Last Chapter

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Ready to make your "last chapter" your best one yet? Embrace your journey, discover new passions, and cherish every moment. Let's celebrate YOU and find profound joy in the years ahead! Sponsored by Brave Transformations.

name: Lunch and Learn - Stuck on the Scale?

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Struggling to lose weight, hit a plateau, or using GLP-1 medications? Join RN and Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist Mindy to learn how your gut microbiome and nervous system influence metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and GLP-1, both naturally and with medication. Connect the dots between (pre) diabetes, food choices, and stubborn weight, and share practical strategies to improve insulin sensitivity. Lunch sponsored by Sugar Shift Solutions.

name: Lunch and Learn - The Impact of Vein Disease

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Have you ever experienced leg pain, swelling, or visible varicose veins? These symptoms may be signs of chronic venous insufficiency, a common but often underdiagnosed condition. Learn typical symptoms associated with varicose vein disease and how ultrasound imaging is used to accurately diagnose and guide treatment. Sponsored by Vein Specialists of Geneva.

name: Lunch and Learn - Why Blood Sugar Matters for Everyone

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Blood sugar affects far more than diabetes alone. RN and Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist Mindy will break down the basics of blood sugar regulation, including the role of the pancreas, liver, and adrenal glands, and explore how both high and low blood sugar can impact energy, metabolism, and overall health. Lunch sponsored by Sugar Shift Solutions.

name: Lunch and Learn -Living Well Your Way

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Planning for the future can feel overwhelming, but you don’t have to navigate it alone. This program provides a practical and supportive overview of important decisions many seniors face, including whether to age in place or explore senior living options. Learn about financial strategies for covering the cost of care and gain guidance on how to plan and manage life transitions with confidence. From understanding your choices to taking the next steps, this session is designed to help you make informed decisions that support your lifestyle, independence, and peace of mind. Sponsored by Presto Real Estate Services.

An Intermediate player understands the strategy, court positioning, can keep score and are likely to be playing tournaments. Players of this level can serve and return but the shot may lack pace, depth or direction. Award presented at the end of the season to the top performer of the league.Competitive players should display consistent and dependable strokes, including directional control and depth on both forehand and backhand shots. Competitive players also have a full understanding of the rules.

name: September Trip - Mean Girls at Paramount

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Based on the iconic Tina Fey film, Mean Girls tells the story of Cady Heron, a sweet and smart new girl who’s just moved from Africa to suburban Illinois. When she enters the wild world of North Shore High, she quickly finds herself tangled up with The Plastics, the school’s most popular – and most ruthless – clique led by queen bee Regina George. As Cady tries to fit in, she learns that popularity comes with a price – and revenge can get ugly fast. Lunch at the Meyer Ballroom before the show. Lunch, show, and transportation included. Aurora.

name: September Trip - Seadog River and Lake Architectural Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Soak in unobstructed views of Chicago’s world-famous architecture from the water with an exciting ride! Start the tour at Navy Pier and sail through the Chicago Harbor Locks to the River’s iconic skyscrapers. Enjoy amusing and informative narration for a fascinating tour through the city’s architectural history as you pass the Civic Opera House, the Merchandise Mart, and the Willis Tower. Buckle up for a short thrilling finale on Lake Michigan to top off your experience and cruise along the skyline at top Seadog speed! Not recommended for travelers with spinal injuries or poor cardiovascular health. Lunch at Navy Pier before the tour. Boat tour and transportation included. Chicago.

name: Shakespeare & Comedy: A Master Class

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 19 yrs

description: Work on comprehending, performing, and mastering heightened text. Stretch and strengthen your comedic chops through a selection of scenes and monologues from some of the bards funniest works: A Midsummer Night’s Dream, Twelfth Night, and more! This class culminates in a final Live Showcase on the last day, where you’ll get to show off your growth to a real audience.

name: Summer Horse Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Giddy up for an unforgettable experience immersed in the world of horses, learning to groom, tack, and handle these majestic animals like a pro. Climb into the saddle and master the basics of riding at the walk and trot. Along the way, discover fascinating facts about horse breeds, colors, and markings, all while enjoying fun games and activities. Make new friends—both human and hoofed—and create memories that will last a lifetime! Wear jeans or Jodhpur pants and boots with a small low heel. Bring an approved riding or bike helmet and a sack lunch.

name: Tai Chi and Qigong for Older Adults - Beginner

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: The simplified 24 step Tai Chi form is practiced for its many health benefits, including improvements in balance, flexibility and range of motion. Consistent practice helps to increase muscle strength and has been shown to benefit those with arthritis and osteoporosis. The gentle, low-impact movements are done slowly with little of no force or tension. The class is suitable for almost anyone and can be adapted to take into consideration most physical limitations.

The circular flowing movements help relieve tension and promote calmness.

Full camp session fee is non-refundable once final payment is collected (one week prior to each camp session).

name: We Hold These Truths by Therese Harrold

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Learning more about politics from hands-on, real-life experience than from academia, Renata Reynolds, an outspoken political science senior, unwittingly turns a class project into a volatile public debate regarding true democracy. Her opponent: an ultra-conservative state congresswoman, Suzanne Nighcore, a University alum and donor. Renata is compelled to ward off possible expulsion at the hand of the private University Chancellor and Representative Nighcore, and to safeguard her goal: a political career in politics. Renata engages the undercover help of the Congresswoman’s estranged son, Rodney. Ultimately, Renata decides to get into the political “game” to learn how to play it if she ever hopes to win based upon her beliefs, her ideals, herself! name: Charleston, SC Diamond Tours

age_range.raw_age_text: 30 yrs +

description: Day 1: Depart your group's location in a spacious, video and restroom equipped motorcoach as you head for your destination: Charleston, South Carolina! This evening you will stay at an en route hotel. Day 2: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast. Today you will continue your journey, then enjoy a leisurely Dinner and check into a Charleston area hotel for a four night stay. Day 3: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll head to historic MIDDLETON PLACE. This impressive attraction contains 65 acres of America's oldest landscaping. After each member receives their welcome map, you'll experience the garden, animal stables, the Chapel, Rice Mill, and more! After lunch on your own and free time in Downtown Charleston, you'll enjoy a scenic HARBOR CRUISE. Enjoy the beauty of the Charleston Harbor and learn the rich history of the "Holy City". During this scenic and relaxing tour, you will see dozens of landmarks and points of interest as hundreds of years of history is covered. This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 4: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy a GUIDED TOUR of McLeod Plantation Historic Site. Established in 1851, this important 37-acre Gullah/Geechee heritage site has been carefully preserved in recognition of its cultural and historical significance. Later, you'll enjoy lunch on your own in the “cultural heart of Charleston.” Next, you'll have some free time to explore The Historic Charleston City Market. Located downtown, this architecturally significant National Historic Landmark is home to eclectic shops, you won't find anywhere else. This continuous series of market buildings stretches four city blocks. Next you'll appreciate a short photo stop at the famed Angel Oak Tree, estimated to be 400 years old! This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 5: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy both a GUIDED TOUR OF CHARLESTON and an intimate TOUR inside the HISTORIC CHARLESTON HOME: The Joseph Manigault House. The Manigault's descent from French Huguenots who fled religious persecution in Europe in the late 1600s. Afterwards, you'll visit the CHARLESTON TEA GARDEN. At this unique tea garden, your group will take a factory tour and see how tea is made, including tasting samples at the Tea Bar. A highlight of your tour includes a TROLLEY TOUR of the garden. This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 6: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast at your hotel before leaving for a visit to the South Carolina State Museum in Columbia, SC. Tonight, you'll relax in an en route hotel. Day 7: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast before departing for home... a perfect time to chat with your friends about all the fun things you've done, the great sights you've seen and where your next group trip will take you! (Sun - Sat) Oct 25 - 31 2026 $1079* WOOD DALE PARK DISTRICT PRESENTS Charleston Motorcoach transportation 6 nights lodging including 4 consecutive nights in the Charleston area 10 meals: 6 breakfasts and 4 dinners Visit to The Historic Charleston City Market Relaxing Harbor Cruise in Charleston Visit to Famous and Historic Middleton Place Guided Tour of Charleston Tour of Historic Charleston Home 'The Joseph Manigault House' Admission to McLeod Plantation Historic Site Photo stop at Famous Angel Oak Tree & Visit to Charleston Tea Garden, Including a Trolley Ride For more pictures, video, and information visit: www.GroupTrips.com/wooddaleparkdistrict Departure: Wood Dale Park District, 111 E Foster Ave, Wood Dale, IL @ 8 am Jen Bolich - Wood Dale

name: Shipshewana, IN. Diamond Tours

age_range.raw_age_text: 30 yrs +

description: Day 1: Depart your group's location in a spacious, video and restroom equipped motorcoach as you head for your destination: Shipshewana, at the heart of Amish Country Indiana! Upon arrival, you will have time for shopping and lunch on your own at the SHIPSHEWANA TRADING PLACE. Consistently ranked one of the top Flea Markets in the Country, offering everything from handmade crafts, unique antiques, and delicious treats. Later, you'll head to Cook's Bison Ranch for an unforgettable experience. Take a SCENIC WAGON TOUR of their majestic ranch while seeing the bison up-close and even feeding them too if you wish! Your tour will conclude at “Buffalo Treasures Gift Shop” to bring home a memento. Next, you'll enjoy Dinner before experiencing the evening show, “LOVES COMES SOFTLY.” Tonight, you'll check into your Shipshewana area hotel for a two-night stay. Day 2: Begin the day by enjoying a Continental Breakfast before departing for a full day GUIDED TOUR of INDIANA'S AMISH COUNTRY. During your tour, you will see local sites such as the famous barn quilts, the Brown-Swiss Dairy Farm Barn, and seasonal gardens, among other important sites in the Shipshewana area. Next, you'll enjoy a visit to downtown Shipshewana, where you'll have lunch on your own and free time for some shopping. Then, your Guided Tour continues with a TOUR OF AN AMISH HOMESTEAD. See the Amish Lifestyle close-up as you tour an Amish Farmhouse. You'll also have an opportunity to experience an expedition to visit an Amish craftsman at work, such as a Furniture Maker, a Rug Weaver, or a Leather Smith. The craftsman will provide a narrated demonstration of their work, focusing on the importance of the craft, and the traditions as it relates to Amish culture. Afterwards, you'll enjoy an AUTHENTIC AMISH DINNER at an Amish Homestead before returning to your hotel. Day 3: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast before Then depart for a visit to MENNO-HOF INTERPRETIVE CENTER. This immersive journey through the Amish and Mennonite story features a guided audio-video presentation and six distinct rooms that provide deep insights into Amish history and beliefs. One of these rooms includes a tornado simulation! You'll gently feel the wind whip and theatre shake as you engage with the powerful experience of nature. You'll have free time to explore additional exhibits at your own pace. Your Countryside Amish Adventure finishes with an exploration of Amish Country Goods at Eash Sales and E & S Foods, located next to each other. This combined one-of-a-kind Amish tailored experience is where you can buy unique Amish foods and see how their culture makes handcrafted home décor. Then depart for home… a perfect time to chat with your friends about all the fun things you've done, the spectacular sights you've seen and where your next group trip will take you! (Tue - Thu) Jul 14 - 16 2026 WOOD DALE PARK DISTRICT AND BENSENVILLE PARK DISTRICT PRESENTS Shipshewana, Indiana Countryside Amish Adventure Motorcoach transportation 2 nights lodging in Indiana 4 meals: 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners FULL DAY GUIDED TOUR OF INDIANA'S AMISH COUNTRY & TOUR OF AN AMISH HOMESTEAD Authentic AMISH HOMESTEAD DINNER Admission to the show “LOVES COMES SOFTLY” at the Blue Gate Theatre Admission to MENNO-HOF, “The Amish & Mennonite Story” Authentic Wagon Tour & Feeding at Cook's Bison Ranch Visit to Nationally Recognized SHIPSHEWANA TRADING PLACE & DOWNTOWN SHIPSHEWANA Explore Amish Country Goods at Eash Sales and E & S Food Departure: Wood Dale Park District, 111 E Foster Ave, Wood Dale, IL @ 8 am Jen Bolich-Wood Dale @ (630) 595-9333 Ty Beshiri-Bensenville @ (630) 766-7015 Award Winning Musical Show Experience a Scenic Bison Wagon Tour Homemade Authentic Amish Dinner Dive into the Amish Culture

name: Coed Beginning II Gymnastics - Session 1

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Tuesday, June 9 2026. Schedule: Tuesdays, 5:30 PM - 6:25 PM , From June 9, 2026 until June 30, 2026 , Chandler Gym Half South , Resource person: gymnastics@cityofevanston.org Location: Chandler Gym Half South (Chandler Newberger Community Center, Chandler Gym) | 1028 Central Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: A coach’s written recommendation is required to register for Beginning II. Beginning II students are required to have taken at least 1 year of consec- utive Beginning (school-age) Gymnastics classes or have had experience in a similar level with another program. They should be able to do a vertical handstand, cartwheel, and roundoff, handstand bridge kickover off a mat, a dive roll vault, and a pullover on bars with a light spot or mat against the wall. They should have experience working on handstands, cartwheels, and dismounts on beam but do not need to be able to do them unassisted. For a complete list of skills, strength, and flexibility requirements or an evaluation please email gymnastics@cityofevanston.org.

name: Juneteenth Celebration

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Friday, June 19 2026. Schedule: Friday, 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM , Dawes Park , Location: Dawes Park | 1700 Sheridan Road, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: This year's "Youthful" Juneteenth Celebration will be a community event that honors the historical legacy of Juneteenth while bringing people together in a spirit of unity, culture, and joy. The celebration recognizes the historic moment in 1865 when the last enslaved African Americans in Galveston, Texas, learned of their freedom and reflects on the continued journey toward freedom and equality for all Americans. This inclusive event welcomes people of all ages and backgrounds to celebrate through vibrant music, dancing, and cultural performances. Making community connections while supporting local food and artisan vendors. Through shared experiences, the Juneteenth Celebration creates a space to honor freedom for all, celebrate multiculturalism, and strengthen the community.

Schedule: Weekdays, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until July 2, 2026 , Robert Crown Gym , Location: Robert Crown Gym (Robert Crown Community Center) | 1801 Main Street, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: Counselor in Training (CIT) Camp prepares teens to work with staff and contribute their talents to the programs offered at the Robert Crown Community Center. Participants serve as role models for the younger children, and receive weekly training from a variety of social service professionals and mentors. The program builds community and prepares youth to work with children in a variety of settings. CIT participants receive basic training on a range of topics: effective engagement, behavior management, communication, team work, safety procedures and more. Senior staff evaluate and mentor the participants throughout the four-week program and provide a final evaluation. Volunteer options include Fun Factory (ages 5-7), or Kid City (ages 7-10). Volunteers are expected to participate in the program Monday through Friday, 9am-4pm for the entire four-week period. Volunteers may speak with the Camp Director to adjust their schedule if necessary. The registration fee includes training and supplies, field trips, and small group activities. Eligible for childcare tax credit. Please note that there is no class on the following date(s): Friday, June 19, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM

name: Youth Aquatic Camp - Morning

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:30 AM - 12:30 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 12, 2026 , Dempster Beach Launch Facility , Resource person: Katie Grundin kgrundin@cityofevanston.org Location: Dempster Beach Launch Facility | 1251 Lake Shore Boulevard, Evanston, IL, 60202 Description: Dive into summer fun at our Aquatic Camp! Campers will rotate through sailing, kayaking, paddleboarding, and tubing, with activities changing based on the day and weather conditions. When they’re not out on the water, they’ll stay active with games like Nukem, capture the flag, relay races, and sandcastle competitions. Please only register for a morning or afternoon session during the same dates. You may register for multiple sessions throughout the summer. Campers are required to pass a 50-yard swim test (any combination of strokes) before they may participate in aquatic activities. Refunds will not be provided if campers are unable to pass the test. Aquatic Camp meets every day, but bad weather, poor conditions or equipment failure may require that activities take place on the sand, a park, or inside the Beach Office. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Jr. Lifeguard Camp - Morning

name: Intermediate Free Skate Camp June 8 - 12, 2026

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Off the ice, campers will participate in conditioning, ballet, yoga, stretching and off-ice skating technique. Participants must have completed all of the Basic Skill levels of the Learn to Skate program. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

Schedule: Every day, 8:00 AM - 3:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 12, 2026 , Resource person: dbengson@cityofevanston.org Description: Designed for HIGH-LEVEL figure skaters, this camp includes both on-ice and off-ice training. On the ice, athletes will focus on power skating, edge work, jumps, jump-harness training, spins, music interpretation and daily indeendent practice sessions. Off the ice, skaters will take part in intense conditioning, cardio training, ballet, yoga, stretching and off-ice jump and positioning technique. Participants must have completed all levels of the Learn to Skate USA program and be able to execute an advanced axel and at least one double jump. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, August 3 2026. The program blends exploration, teamwork, and career-ready skills to inspire the next generation of aerospace innovators. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Amigos Adventure Camp 2026 Session 1

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Every day, 8:30 AM - 12:30 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 18, 2026 , Dawes Elementary , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Dawes Elementary | 440 Dodge Avenue, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: A fun and active Spanish Summer Camp where kids learn the language through play,                   swimming, and outdoor adventures while making friends and building confidence. ✨ ¡Vamos a Aprender! Spanish Immersion Camp ✨ Get ready for a summer full of movement, creativity, and language learning! Our Spanish Immersion Camp brings the language to life through games, music, storytelling, dance, and exciting field trips —making learning fun, active, and unforgettable. 📍 Location: Dawes Elementary School 440 Dodge Ave, Evanston, IL 60202 Through the Total Physical Response (TPR) approach, campers don’t just learn Spanish—they experience it. By combining language with physical movement and interactive play, children naturally build vocabulary, confidence, and comprehension in a way that feels like fun, not work. 🌟 What to Expect: High-energy games that reinforce Spanish vocabulary Music, dance, and cultural exploration Interactive storytelling and creative expression Hands-on learning experiences and field trips A supportive, engaging environment for all learners Whether your child is brand new to Spanish or already has some experience, this camp is designed to spark curiosity, build confidence, and make language learning joyful . 🎉 Come ready to move, laugh, and learn—¡nos vemos pronto! Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 1: Aviation)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 8 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 8, 2026 until June 12, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: The Maccstream STEM and Aviation module offers Camp Flight participants a focused, hands-on experience where science, technology, engineering, and mathematics come to life through real application. Over the course of one week, students explore core concepts in physics and aerodynamics, use block coding to animate characters and program drones, and engage with flight simulators to understand the mechanics of aviation. They are introduced to different engineering pathways and challenged to design and build solutions that meet specific criteria, all while using practical math skills—measurement, geometry, probability, and algebra—to complete meaningful tasks. Beyond technical exposure, the experience builds problem-solving, critical thinking, and confidence. Students learn how to approach challenges with structure and creativity, while gaining insight into real-world careers in STEM and aviation. The module closes with intentional reflection, where participants assess their growth, set clear goals, and map out next steps. It becomes more than a workshop—it is a bridge between curiosity and direction, helping young people see how what they learn today can shape where they go next. Eligible for childcare tax credit.
