name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 2: Debate)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 15 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 15, 2026 until June 18, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: In Debate, students learn to slow their thinking down just enough to make it sharp. This is not about arguing loudly or trying to win at all costs. It is about learning how to see an issue clearly, build a position with purpose, and communicate in a way that earns respect. Students engage real-world topics that connect to their lives—community, technology, culture—and practice organizing their thoughts, supporting ideas with evidence, and listening closely to understand different perspectives without losing their own voice. Each session blends reflection, skill-building, and live practice through structured debates and guided dialogue. Along the way, students strengthen their ability to think critically, speak confidently, and manage emotions under pressure. The environment is grounded in respect and accountability, where every voice matters and every idea must stand on reason. By the end, students carry more than debate skills—they carry a way of thinking and communicating that will serve them in school, work, and everyday life. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 4: Theater)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, June 29 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From June 29, 2026 until July 2, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Theater: Express Yourself: Acting FUNdamentals is an engaging, confidence-building theatre class that uses play, movement, voice, and storytelling to strengthen communication and self-expression skills. Through exciting theatre games, vocal warm-ups, and performance activities inspired by master practitioners including Viola Spolin, Kristin Linklater, Michael Shurtleff, Stanislavski, and others, students explore the foundational acting tools of body, voice, focus, and imagination. Classes are thoughtfully designed to meet students developmentally while maintaining shared creative goals. By the end of the program, students will feel more confident expressing themselves authentically, speak more clearly and audibly while strengthening the physical voice, connect emotion to vocal expression, and work more comfortably in groups with increased focus and collaboration, and have gained a mini-canon of classic poems and stories. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 7:  Science Fair Tinkering)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, July 20 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From July 20, 2026 until July 24, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Science Fair Tinkering – Go STEM For two weeks, Camp Flight is proud to partner with Go STEM Chicago to engage campers in a hands-on, inquiry-driven science fair experience. Through this partnership, students move beyond worksheets and simulations and into real investigation—asking questions, testing ideas, and building projects that reflect how science and problem-solving show up in the real world. Go STEM facilitators guide campers through the full science fair process: developing a question, conducting research, designing experiments, analyzing results, and preparing a clear, confident presentation of their findings. Students work independently and collaboratively, learning how to think critically, revise their ideas, and communicate their work to others. The two-week arc allows for depth rather than rush, reinforcing Camp Flight’s belief that sustained curiosity, thoughtful iteration, and public sharing are where real learning—and real confidence—take root. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

name: Camp FLIGHT (Week 9: Culinary)

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Monday, July 27 2026. Schedule: Every day, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM , From July 27, 2026 until July 31, 2026 , Gibbs-Morrison Cafe , Resource person: Harrington Gibson Location: Gibbs-Morrison Cafe (Gibbs-Morrison Cultural Center) | 1823 Church Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Culinary Week invites Camp Flight participants into the practice of nourishment as both skill and responsibility. Students explore how to prepare simple, healthy meals while learning the foundations of nutrition, food safety, and kitchen confidence. A central thread of the experience is self-sufficiency—understanding how to select, prepare, and combine ingredients in ways that support the body and mind. Whenever possible, meals are created using what students have harvested themselves, connecting the full cycle from soil to plate. Beyond cooking, the week builds awareness and discipline. Participants begin to see how their food choices impact energy, focus, and overall well-being. They learn to plan, collaborate, and adapt, gaining practical life skills that extend far beyond the kitchen. Culinary Week becomes more than preparing meals—it is about cultivating independence, respect for resources, and the ability to sustain oneself with intention. Eligible for childcare tax credit.

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Saturday, May 23 2026. Schedule: Saturday, 7:00 PM - 9:00 PM , Noyes Street Theatre , Location: Noyes Street Theatre (Noyes Cultural Arts Center) | 927 Noyes Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: Gee's Bend is the story of the Pettway women, quilters from the isolated community of Gee's Bend, Alabama. Beginning in 1939, the play follows Alice, her daughters Sadie and Nella, and Sadie's husband, Macon, through segregation, family strife, and the Civil Rights movement. Throughout their lives, the women's extraordinary quilts provide a respite from the turmoil around them. In the last act of the play, it is the year 2000; the quilts have been discovered as folk art and have become very valuable. Sadie is pleased with the recognition, but despite the lure of the big city, she returns to Gee's Bend and continues to quilt. Wilder's play explores the resilience of the human spirit, especially as it is expressed in art. No Transfer/Refunds
